title: feat(gcode): add the camcraft-gcode reader crate for 3-axis RS-274 and ISO 6983 programs
body:
## What this PR does

This PR adds the new crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`). The crate reads RS-274/NGC and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs. It gives `cl::Toolpath` sections and a 1-based line map. It refuses unsupported words by name and line number.

- The crate depends on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry` and `thiserror` only.
- It decodes the modal groups, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs in `G17`/`G18`/`G19`, and the canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98`/`G99` and `L`.
- It splits sections at `T`/`M6`. It reads `S`, `M3`-`M5`, `M0`-`M2`, `M30`, `G4`, `G61`, `G64`, `G53`, `G28` and `G30`.
- It refuses `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, a missing `G20`/`G21`, a missing reference position, and `A`/`B`/`C`.

Sources: RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556), ISO 6983, and the public controller documents that `crates/gcode/src/dialect.rs` names for the dwell and arc presets. No other parser code was used.

## Held work

- Commit `711314efd` by Mike Kinney, from `mkinney:issue/2217-camcraft-gcode`. It has the crate, its 9 tests, the decision file and the gate plan entries.
- This PR keeps that commit and its author unchanged. A merge commit (`db23cf9bd`) joins it to main `60376ccbb`.

## Added after the held commit

- `db23cf9bd` merge: the conflict resolution (next section).
- `75b33ace3` `test(xtask)`: two xtask tests of main list the crates by hand. `heavy_plan_tests::reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies` now expects `gcode` in the reach of `geometry`. `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep` now writes a stub `crates/gcode`. `Cargo.lock` takes the version `0.25.0` for `camcraft-gcode`.
- `92627aef0` `test(gcode)`:
  - Each gcode suite has a `Gate map: covers camcraft_gcode::{..}` line. Quick then selects the suites for a change in each `crates/gcode/src` module.
  - The new suite `degenerate_input` checks malformed programs. Each one gives a value or a refusal, with no panic and no hang.
  - The decision file records the merge.

## Conflict resolution

All three conflicts were lists. No logic hunk had a conflict.

- Root `Cargo.toml`: the `members` line has main's `"crates/gpu"` and the held `"crates/gcode"` (after `"crates/cl"`). The `camcraft-gcode` workspace dependency merged without a conflict.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs`: `BATCH_CRATES`, `ALL_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` have `"gcode"` after `"cl"` and main's `"gpu"` after `"app"`.
- `xtask/src/tests.rs`: the release step count keeps main's known-fail `checks` term. It uses the held `plan::ALL_CRATES.len()` in place of the fixed `10`.
- `Cargo.lock` merged without a conflict.

## New crate edges

- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-cl`: `ArcPlane`, `Cycle`, `CycleKind`, `MoveKind`, `PathBuilder`, `Toolpath`, `lattice`.
- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-geometry`: `geo2d::Point2`, `Point3`, `units::{from_display, Unit, MM_PER_INCH}`.
- `docs/decisions/2217-camcraft-gcode.md` gives the imported items, the reason that a caller cannot pass the values in, and the rebuild impact. No crate depends on `camcraft-gcode` yet.

## Tests

- `gcode_3axis`:
  - `modal_groups_track_and_sections_split_on_tool_changes`
  - `ijk_and_r_arcs_xy_xz_yz_and_full_circle`
  - `r_major_vs_minor_arc_centers_differ_as_expected`
  - `canned_cycles_expand_into_move_chains_and_honor_g98_g99`
  - `unit_scaling_g20_inches_to_mm_and_unscaled_s_t_p`
  - `reference_moves_g53_g28_g30_execute_when_configured_and_refuse_when_missing`
  - `unsupported_codes_and_bad_inputs_refuse_by_name_with_line_number`
- `dialects_and_planes`:
  - `vertical_plane_r_arcs_xz_and_yz_minor_and_major`
  - `dialects_dwell_units_ream_and_m6_tool_order`
- `degenerate_input` (new): `degenerate_programs_refuse_or_parse_without_panic_or_hang`

## Gate

All results are on head `92627aef0`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the batch plan, because `Cargo.lock` changed. Result: 1133 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled. The failed step is `clippy -D warnings` in `camcraft-gpu`. See "Known red step".
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gcode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass, 0 warnings.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-gcode`:
  - `gcode_3axis`: 7 passed.
  - `dialects_and_planes`: 2 passed.
  - `degenerate_input`: 1 passed.
  - 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 295 passed in the lib test binary. The 6 other test binaries passed. 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 3 steps, 0 failed.
- Full heavy lanes: not run. The rule of #3556 keeps them for the cut.

## Known red step

The failed quick step is not caused by this PR.

- The error: `the loop variable a is used to index dims` at `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs:126` (`clippy::needless_range_loop`), in `camcraft-gpu`.
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` lists no file in `crates/gpu`.
- The loop `for a in 0..3` is at the same line in `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs` on the merge base `60376ccbb` and on `origin/main` `f2b2369ed`. The file has no change between the two.
- No open issue or PR tracks it. Issue #1624 is a closed case of the same lint in another crate. The open issue #3524 is a different red check on main.
- The `camcraft-gcode` crate passes clippy with `-D warnings` alone.

## Not exercised

- No caller uses the crate yet. The post round trip and the simulator are in the follow-up issues.
- The controller presets (`fanuc`, `haas`, `tormach`, `grblhal`, `tinyg`, `carvera`) were not compared with a real controller.
- A heavy lane is not required: the crate has no heavy test.

## Unblocks

#2218, #2219, #2222, #2227

Process change: yes

Changelog: Added the `camcraft-gcode` crate. It reads RS-274/NGC and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs into toolpath sections with a 1-based line map, and refuses unsupported codes by name and line number.

Effort: max

Fixes #2217

title: fix(motion): 2D Adaptive keeps the full tool clear of "Do not touch" items
body:
## What changed

"Do not touch" now applies to 2D Adaptive operations, with the Spiral method and with the Trochoidal method. Before this change, the operation refused the protected items.

- `do_not_touch_applies` accepts `OpType::Adaptive2D`. The refusal text, the MCP tool description and the guide name 2D Adaptive with Trace (#3348), 2D Offset, 3D Pocket and Face (#3343).
- The new module `machining2d::adaptive_avoid` gives one law to the two methods:
  - The keep-out is one region. It covers each tip height from the floor up to the clearance plane. Thus it holds every cut, every entry and every descent of the path, for the flutes, the shank and the holder.
  - The planner removes that region from its cutter-centre area. Then it plans as it does without protection. The crossing law, the entry and link certificates and the Offset-rings fallback (Spiral) or the move check (Trochoidal) read the reduced area.
  - Rapid links are lifted over the items (`elevate_rapid_links`). A link that cannot clear them refuses the operation.
  - A corner relief that enters the keep-out refuses the operation, as on 2D Offset.
  - When no item reaches the region, both methods call the plain planner. The path does not change.
- **Pass starts at** (#3355) is read on the protected Spiral path too (`adaptive_spiral_avoid_on`). The Trochoidal method still refuses Inside and Outside by name.
- The generic checks in `generate.rs` (`route_links`, `verify_avoid`) and the post gate (`live_avoid_problems`) already read each kind that `do_not_touch_applies` accepts. They have no change.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3346-adaptive2d-do-not-touch.md` (with the dropped options).

**Known cost:** 2D Adaptive plans one area for all levels. Beside a protected item that is lower than the top of the cut, it leaves more stock than 2D Offset, which keeps out level by level. The guide says so. This costs cut area. It does not cost safety.

## Merge of main

The branch merges `upstream/main` three times:

- `1d1bd090f` (main `6cfc0a6d4`): conflicts with #3343 (Face) in `do_not_touch_applies`, its refusal text, the MCP description, the UI test and the guide. Both sides are kept. A conflict with #3355 in the 2D Adaptive arm of `generate.rs` is resolved by commit `067a914a1`, which threads the `StartSide` into the protected Spiral path.
- `f73493967` (main `74ea8988d`): no conflict.
- `241f6aeb5` (main `f35202134`): conflicts with #3348 (Trace) in `do_not_touch_applies`, its refusal text, the MCP description and the UI test. Both sides are kept: the list is now "Trace, 2D Offset, 2D Adaptive, 3D Pocket and Face". Main also removed "only so far" from the refusal text. Thus the 2D Adaptive UI test now checks that no "is supported on" note shows. The old check looked for text that main no longer writes.

## Pinning tests

- motion `avoid_adaptive`:
  - `a_spiral_adaptive_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_of_a_protected_pin_with_no_crossing`
  - `a_spiral_adaptive_with_no_keepout_on_the_region_is_the_plain_path`
  - `a_spiral_adaptive_with_a_pass_start_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_of_a_protected_pin`
  - `a_trochoidal_adaptive_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_of_a_protected_pin`
  - `an_empty_avoid_gives_the_plain_trochoidal_path`
  - `a_trochoidal_adaptive_with_no_room_left_is_refused_with_the_item_named`
- app `do_not_touch_adaptive`:
  - `adaptive2d_do_not_touch_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_and_clears_back_to_the_plain_path`
  - `adaptive2d_with_no_room_clear_of_the_protection_is_refused_with_the_item_named`
  - `adaptive2d_do_not_touch_round_the_tower_at_the_default_load_posts` (heavy lane)
- ui `do_not_touch`:
  - `adaptive2d_shows_the_pick_protected_button_and_no_unsupported_note`
  - `unsupported_op_shows_do_not_touch_note_without_pick_button` (new text)

## Gates

On `241f6aeb5` (the head of this PR):

- Quick gate (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 769 steps, 0 failed, 1 stalled. The stalled step is `ui suites: lib`: it gave no output for 15 min. The cause is local: on the author's machine the NVIDIA Vulkan driver hangs in `vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties` while it waits for an X server reply (`vulkaninfo` hangs too). Each GPU lib test hangs there, and the #3589 lock holds the other GPU tests behind it. A rerun of that step alone with `DISPLAY` unset (`--only "ui suites: lib"`) passed: 1493 tests, 91 s.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 253 steps, 0 failed, 56.6 min. Four known fails were red as expected (#1950 three times, #2849 one time).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Without `--no-deps`, clippy stops in `camcraft-gpu` (`needless_range_loop`). This branch does not change that crate, and main has the same code.

Earlier runs:

- On `f73493967`: quick gate 765 steps, 0 failed (one stall in `app build (--no-run)`, which passed alone). Heavy lanes 252 steps, 0 failed.
- On `067a914a1`: one failure, `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`. Main's #3464 left `examples/first-router-part.nc` stale, and main fixed it in `74a87c662`. The merge `f73493967` brings that fix.

## Not exercised

- No machine air cut.
- No per-level keep-out. A level above a low protected item loses the same area as the floor level.

Changelog: 2D Adaptive (Spiral and Trochoidal) honours "Do not touch": the full tool (flutes, shank, holder) stays clear of each protected face or edge by the clearance, or the operation is refused with the item named.

Fixes #3346

title: fix(build): pin the text files that tests read to LF
body:
## Cause

Tests read tracked text files and search them for text that holds a line break. Git for Windows checks out text with CRLF when `core.autocrlf=true`. The search then fails. `.gitattributes` pinned only the golden, fixture and program trees to LF (#2840).

## Change

Three rules in `.gitattributes`, in the style of the existing rules:

```
AGENTS.md text eol=lf
site/**/*.md text eol=lf
crates/post/tests/klartext/contour.cnc text eol=lf
```

Reader of each tree:
- `AGENTS.md`: `xtask/src/light_tests.rs:137` (through `scan::read`) and `xtask/src/heavy_plan_tests.rs:207-212` (`include_str!`).
- `site/**/*.md`: `xtask/src/catalog_links_tests.rs:100-108` and `xtask/src/catalog_tests.rs:137,241,244`.
- `crates/post/tests/klartext/contour.cnc`: `crates/post/tests/script_heidenhain_klartext.rs:197` (and `comment_escape.rs:239` includes it).

## Readings

Each matched file is `i/lf` before the rule, so no blob changes (`git ls-files --eol`). `git status --short` shows only `.gitattributes`.

Command per file: `rm <file> && git -c core.autocrlf=true checkout -- <file> && git ls-files --eol <file>`.

| File | Before the rule | After the rule |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | `i/lf w/crlf` | `i/lf w/lf` |
| `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md` | `i/lf w/crlf` | `i/lf w/lf` |
| `crates/post/tests/klartext/contour.cnc` | `i/lf w/crlf` | `i/lf w/lf` |

`git check-attr text eol` after the rule: `text: set`, `eol: lf` for the three files. Before the rule: `unspecified`.

## Decision (recorded here, no decision file)

- Taken: targeted LF pins for the text trees that a test reads.
- Dropped: one global `* text=auto eol=lf`. It would renormalise seven `.rs` files that hold real CR bytes. It would also change the checkout of every contributor in one step. This is too wide for this issue.
- Dropped: a change of the xtask readers. It is a process-file change and covers only the named readers.
- Left out: `docs/**/*.md` and `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`. No test reads their content (the `docs/` paths in tests are names and in-memory fixtures). Add a rule when a test starts to read one.
- Not in this PR: `crates/app/tests/docs_troubleshooting.rs:26`. It joins `\`-newline strings from `.rs` sources. That is #3619, a separate PR. The fix there is in the test reader, because `.rs` files cannot be pinned without renormalising the seven CR files.

## Not exercised

No build ran. The change is attribute lines. On an LF checkout nothing changes.

## Contributor with an existing CRLF checkout

Git does not rewrite files that already exist. Run this in a clean tree:

```
git rm --cached -r AGENTS.md site crates/post/tests/klartext/contour.cnc
git reset --hard
```

Or check out those files again.

Fixes #3553

title: test(motion): pin that a hole tilted from the tool axis is not drilled along Z
body:
This PR takes the pin test that the agent of mkinney wrote for #3554 (branch `mkinney:issue/3554-tilted-hole-pin`, commit `418e88034`). The coordinator opens it; the commit and its author do not change.

**What #3554 asked:** check if a hole that is tilted some degrees from the tool axis is recognized as a Z hole and drilled along Z. That would be a wrong cut.

**Result (issue comment of 2026-11-22T19:29Z):** it is not. The circle fit in `classify` (`recognize.rs`) uses the wall vertices of the top and of the bottom of the hole. A tilt of 2 degrees over 10 mm moves the section centre by 0.35 mm, the fit residual is near 0.17 mm, and `FIT_TOL` (0.02 mm) refuses the wall. A short tilted hole can pass; then `FIT_TOL` limits the wall movement to 0.02 mm, the same tolerance as each tessellated hole.

**The tests** (`crates/motion/src/drilling/tests_tilted.rs`):
- `tilted_wall_builder_at_zero_tilt_is_a_z_hole`: the fixture at 0 degrees gives one Z hole.
- `tilted_holes_in_a_plate_are_not_drilled_along_z`: a 10 mm plate with holes tilted 2 and 5 degrees (also -2 degrees, and 1, 2 and 8 bands): no Z hole and no cross hole.
- `a_tilt_the_fit_accepts_moves_no_wall_past_fit_tol`: thin walls with a small tilt; where the fit accepts one, each wall vertex is within `FIT_TOL` of the circle.

Mutation by the author: with `FIT_TOL` set to 0.5 the second test fails; with 0.02 it passes.

**Not in this PR:** a tilted hole is dropped with no named message. A named skip is an enhancement, not a defect.

No product code changes. `Changelog: none`

Fixes #3554

title: docs(mcp): skill row for pass_start on every kind that has it
body:
## What changed

One row of `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` (the "Pass starts at (#3316)" row). The row said that other kinds get the key in their own issues. Those issues are merged. The row now says:

- The key `pass_start` is on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, Circular, Bore, 3D Pocket and 3D Finish, and on 2D Offset (already in the row). It uses the same `edit_operation` door.
- Absent means `"auto"`. The project file does not write `"auto"`. The reply leaves it out.
- Where the choice is not used, the app says so. 2D Pocket with Zigzag rows or with rest machining carries a `Pass starts at` note. 3D Pocket carries it with the Zigzag or Auto strategy, with rest machining, or with the Adaptive (HSM) strategy. A 3D Finish reads the key only for Contour and Flat; the op page says that the other patterns have no ring order.
- 2D Adaptive with the Trochoidal method refuses `"inside"` and `"outside"` by name, at the edit and again at `generate`.
- Face, Slot and Trochoidal Slot refuse the key by name. Any other kind refuses it as an unknown field.

## Source lines that prove each statement

- Field on the kinds: `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs` (Pocket, Adaptive2D, Offset2D, Circular, Pocket3D, Finish3D, Bore).
- Values `auto` / `inside` / `outside`, default Auto: `crates/app/src/project/pass_start_dto.rs:15-20`.
- The reply leaves `auto` out: `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:326-327` (the reply is the written params). Lines 111-113 of the same file serve only the internal unknown-field check.
- Refusal by name for Face, Slot, Trochoidal Slot: `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:65-75`.
- Unknown field on other kinds: the round-trip check in `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` (`pass_start_kept`).
- Trochoidal refusal: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm_start.rs:70-77`. It is called at the edit by `named_refusal` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs:87`, from `crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs:114`) and at `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:902`. Pinned by `trochoidal_adaptive_refuses_a_forced_pass_start_by_name` in `crates/app/tests/adaptive_pass_start.rs`.
- Notes: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs` (Zigzag, rest), `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:329`, `crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_side.rs:19-20, 34-41` (3D Pocket cases), `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (2D rest note).
- 3D Finish reads only Contour and Flat: `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/shadow.rs:259-262`; op page text in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mill3d_page.rs`.

## Not done here

The issue also asks for a row in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`. That file is generated and has no `pass_start` text. The generic `edit_operation` door has no per-kind rows there. A hand edit of a generated file is not possible, so this PR does not change it.

No build ran: the change is text in one skill file.

Effort: low

Fixes #3569

title: fix(multiaxis): Rotary Parallel cuts the full turn of the bar
body:
## Cause (measured)

Rotary Parallel ran the 3-axis swarf raster one time, in a frame that lays the rotary axis down with local z up. That raster finishes the bar from above only. Two stages lose the bottom of the bar:

1. The ring ladder stops at Bottom, read as a tip height in the laid frame. With Bottom at -R, the last ring has its ball centre 30 degrees under the horizontal.
2. With a lower Bottom, the rings stop 45 degrees under the horizontal. `build_sups` turns each facet normal to the sky, so the bottom quadrant counts as shallow (raster) ground. The raster takes the top tangent and never reaches that ground. The rings skip loops that touch only shallow facets.

A third fault hid the band: the rotary path dropped the raster and ring notes on the default path.

## Measured arc

Laid bar R 3 mm, 1 mm ball, Bottom -R (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_coverage.rs`):

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| stepover 0.8 | 126 deg uncut, 210..336 deg (270 = bottom); 4 empty 30-degree sectors | 0 empty sectors; widest gap 12.1 deg |
| stepover 0.25 | 126 deg uncut, the same arc | 0 empty sectors; widest gap 8.1 deg |

With Bottom at -R-2r (stage 2 only), the uncut arc was 94.6 deg. The example part (Journal, Bottom 9.525 mm under the axis) is held by stage 2: about 90 deg, a quarter of the turn. The issue said 10-20 %.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary.rs`: Rotary Parallel plans the bar in two halves. Half A is the laid frame. Half B is the same frame turned half a turn about the axis.
- New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/halves.rs`:
  - Each half keeps the cut over its own upper half.
  - Half B goes back into A's frame by the rigid half turn.
  - The seam: A keeps centres down to half a ball radius under the axis plane. B keeps only centres strictly under A's lowest kept centre, on each side, read over the turned surface. No pass is cut twice. The seam step is one ring step (6.4 deg on the fixture).
  - Half B is held to Bottom where the radially posed ball touches the bar. A Bottom above the axis thus keeps the cut to the upper arc, as before.
  - The lifts of half B become links, so the radial relink rebuilds them along the radius.
- Review rework (head `864897476`): no cut of the single-frame path is lost on a part that is not round, and no place is cut twice:
  - A cut of half A under the seam stays where no kept cut of half B stands at the same place (a ball centre within half a pass spacing). Example: the lower wall of a keyway, which half B cannot see.
  - A cut of half B over the seam is added where half A cuts nothing at the same place (a wall that faces down).
  - The pass spacing is the stepover, or the scallop step `sqrt(8 r tol)`, the larger.
  - New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/gaps.rs`: the ball-centre cover (a grid hash) and a reach reading on a fixed grid of at most 48 stations x 72 angles. A ray from the axis finds the outermost surface. A place under Bottom, or a corner where no ball fits, is skipped. A place with no ball centre within one pass spacing gets the note `Rotary Parallel: no pass reaches the surface over <a0>..<a1> deg about the axis (from the top of the laid bar toward its +y side) at stations <s0>..<s1> mm along it - that surface stays uncut`. Only a path with no such place has the full-turn note.
  - Round bars keep their output: `rotary_coverage` and the example program are byte-identical to the first head.
  - If half B fails with an error other than `Empty`, the whole operation is refused (also where the single-frame path posts). The refusal is visible. This is recorded in the decision file.
- All base notes (raster, rings) now reach the path. A path that cuts under the axis has the note `Rotary Parallel: the passes go all the way round the bar - the machine must turn the part on a rotary axis through the whole turn; set Bottom above the axis to cut only the upper arc`.
- No change to `build_sups` or to any shared finishing helper. The planning time of Rotary Parallel is about two times the old time.

A ball sphere that is clear of the model stays clear under a rigid rotation. The radial pose keeps every ball centre. So each half is as safe as the old single run. The new moves go through the existing held-end clip, picked-face clip, radial relink (no rapid through the part) and radial pose.

## Goldens that moved

Only the two Rotary Parallel programs that had the band moved. The review rework moved neither of them again.

**`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`** (the microARC test part, Bottom -R): regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test microarc_test_part`. Lines 3246 -> 2684, G1 2924 -> 2191, G0 226 -> 415; diff +1333 / -1895. The feed moves that turn A, binned in 30-degree A sectors: before `187 154 122 108 436 319 328 472 97 116 148 186`, after `187 154 122 116 148 186 187 154 122 116 148 186`. The two halves now give the same cut in each half turn. The first head did not run this binary.

**The example:** It was regenerated with the test's own tool (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part`). No hand edits.

| `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | 3125 | 2866 |
| G1 lines | 1662 | 1508 |
| G0 lines | 1398 | 1300 |
| Mid-journal feed endpoints in each 30-degree A sector | 31 30 3 5 11 0 0 9 5 3 16 30 | 31 30 3 3 16 30 31 30 3 3 16 30 |

- Diff: `.nc` +1426 / -1685 lines, `.camproj` +8531 / -12275 lines.
- The program has fewer lines: the deep rings of the old single frame (under the equator) go, and half B cuts the bottom with raster lines.
- The start and the end are as before: the same header, the same T1 change, the first `G53 G0 Z0` then `G0 A44.604`, the same first passes, then `G94`, a G0 retract, `M9`, `M5`, `G53 G0 Z0`, `M30`.
- The guide page `first-continuous-4axis-part.md`, its two toolpath pictures (made again by `site/tools/first_continuous_4axis_pictures.py`) and its pins in `site/tests/test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py` follow the new program: the line count, the excerpts, the A range -85.708..265.687, the last A, the A180 line and the second note.
- No non-rotary golden moved. `golden_cl`, `example_catalog*`, `first_part_programs` and the finish3d suites are green with no change. No shipped example or catalog case uses Rotary Parallel on a machine with limited rotary travel.

## Maintainer decision (owner's standing word 2026-11-22: choose recommended while he sleeps)

1. The example is regenerated with the test's own tool. Dropped: hand edits.
2. `operations::rotary_parallel_generates_radial_axes_and_verifies_clean`:
   - Old assert (main): every cut tip, read as a vertical ball in the laid frame, is not under Bottom (`lowest >= -4`).
   - First head: `a >= -4 || b >= -4`. The review found this vacuous, because `b` holds for each move under the axis.
   - New assert (review rework): over the axis plane only half A cuts, and each feed and plunge there keeps A's own law (`low >= -4`). Under the axis plane each one keeps B's law in B's frame. Every feed and plunge of either half touches at or over the Bottom in world z (`tip z >= -4.1`, a real bound). Both halves cut more than 20 moves. Each 30-degree sector holds a pass. The "last line IS the Bottom" assert stays.
   - Dropped: the old one-frame law, because it pinned the band.
3. Limited rotary travel (`tilthead.mch`, B -120..120): a full-turn path is refused by the machine check. The check names the move, the axis, the angle and the travel, and nothing posts. The way to the reachable arc is a Bottom above the axis: the existing tilt-head fixture (Bottom 1) posts clean with no change. New pin: `a_full_turn_rotary_parallel_refuses_on_a_head_that_cannot_reach_under`. The clean post on a 4-axis A machine is `continuous_4axis_part` (microARC 4). Dropped: clipping the cut to the machine's reach in the generator, because the generator does not know the machine. Follow-up: #3649 (a parameter for the angular range).

The decision file is `docs/decisions/2970-rotary-parallel-halves.md`. Also dropped: the `build_sups` change of the earlier plan, because it changes every 3D pattern and makes the split depend on the mesh winding.

## Pins

- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_coverage.rs`:
  - `the_rotary_parallel_goes_all_the_way_round_a_laid_bar`
  - `the_rotary_parallel_goes_all_the_way_round_at_a_fine_stepover`
  - These two tests check the empty sectors, the seam step against the flank, no pass cut twice, no move emitted twice, and the full-turn note. Both are red on main.
  - `the_rotary_parallel_keeps_the_ladder_notes` (a `rings:` note reaches the path)
  - `a_bottom_over_the_axis_keeps_the_cut_to_the_upper_arc`
- `crates/app/tests/operations.rs`: `rotary_parallel_generates_radial_axes_and_verifies_clean` (sector coverage added; verifies clean with stock)
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs`: `a_full_turn_rotary_parallel_refuses_on_a_head_that_cannot_reach_under`
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/single_frame_tests.rs` (review rework; in `--lib`). The reference is the generator before the halves (laid swarf, radial relink, radial pose), kept for tests only:
  - `a_keyway_loses_no_cut_of_the_single_frame_path`: keyed bar R 10, keyway walls at z = +-5, 6 mm ball. Before the rework, 52 centre samples that the single frame cuts were lost (stations 23.7..36.3 mm, 347 deg: the lower keyway wall). After the rework, 0 are lost.
  - `a_keyway_is_cut_once_in_each_place`: no two passes that are not neighbours stand within 0.1 mm.
  - `the_reach_reading_names_the_arc_no_pass_reaches`: the arc and stations are named. No note for a full turn, and no note for a Bottom over the axis.
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_parallel_keyway.rs` (new): the keyed bar in bar stock. The only blocking finding is the keyway corner rest that a 6 mm ball cannot reach (envelope gouge 0.020 mm, rest 1.95 mm). The single-frame path reports the same finding (gouge 0.020, rest 1.99). Both halves cut. Each rapid ends on the clearance cylinder. The full-turn note is there.
- Not covered: an eccentric section (a round collar off the axis). The axis fit refuses every variant that was tried ("every axis fits this model equally"), so no such part reaches Rotary Parallel. The decision file records this gap in the evidence.

## Gate (final head `864897476`, after `git merge origin/main`, debug, by name)

- motion: `--lib` (570), `--no-run`, `rotary_coverage`, `rotary`, `rotary_offset`, `rotary_links`, `rotary_adaptive`, `rotary_contour_x`, `rotary_dflat`, `swarf_pose_continuity`, `swarf_reentry`, `multiaxis`, `multiaxis_rough`, `refusal_ghost_frames`: all green. The first head also ran `finish3d`, `finish3d_gaplink`, `finish3d_holes`, `finish3d_land`, `finish3d_overhang_and_chord` and `scallop_ceiling` green. The rework does not touch their code.
- app: `--lib` (300), `rotary_parallel_keyway`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `first_4axis_part`, `first_part_programs`, `rotary_verify`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn`, `mcp_rotary_stack`, `opening_rotary_pose`, `rotary_contour_x`, `rotary_face_selection`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `rotary_field_parity`, `rotary_fixtures`, `rotary_letter`, `rotary_subplate`, `rotary_subplate_standing`, `wire_4axis`, `first_traverse_posed`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `coarse_laws`, `microarc_test_part` (after its golden was regenerated), `probe_op`, `project_roundtrip`, `setup_align_multiaxis`, `operations`, `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `posting`, `verify`, `mcp`, `docs_troubleshooting`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: all green.
- clippy `-D warnings`: motion `--all-targets`, app `--lib --test operations --test rotary_parallel_keyway --test rotary_verify`: clean.
- site: `PYTHONUTF8=1 python -m unittest discover -s site/tests -p test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py`: OK.

## Not run

- No heavy lane (P3). No light lane.
- No app window. No machine or simulator run.
- Not tested: an eccentric section (the axis fit refuses it). The reach reading reads only the outermost surface along each radial. A wall hidden behind other material along the radial is not read.

Changelog: Rotary Parallel now cuts the full turn of a bar when Bottom is at its underside (before, about a quarter of the turn at the bottom stayed uncut with no warning); a Bottom above the axis keeps the cut to the upper arc, and the path notes say when the passes go all the way round.

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(examples): pin the catalog refusal.txt files to LF
body:
Cause: `.gitattributes` pins `examples/**/*.nc` to LF. No rule covers `examples/catalog/**/refusal.txt`. The test `example_catalog` compares the refusal lines byte for byte. A checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` writes CRLF, and two tests fail (`catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::regenerates` and `::rebuilds`).

Change: one rule in `.gitattributes`, next to the `.nc` rule, in the same form (`text eol=lf`):

    examples/catalog/**/refusal.txt text eol=lf

Readings (checkout of the file with `-c core.autocrlf=true`, in a worktree):

- Before the rule: `git ls-files --eol` shows `i/lf w/crlf attr/`.
- After the rule: `git ls-files --eol` shows `i/lf w/lf attr/text eol=lf`.
- `git check-attr text eol` shows `text: set` and `eol: lf`.
- There is one `refusal.txt` under `examples/catalog`. It is `i/lf w/lf` after the change.
- `git status` shows only `.gitattributes` changed. No blob changes.

No build ran: the change is one attribute line. The `example_catalog` suite is green on LF checkouts (post-merge runs).

Not widened: the other text files under `examples/catalog` (`case.toml`, `build.camscript`, `*.camproj`, `*.md`, `*.obj`, `*.py`) have no rule. They are LF in the index. No failure is known for them. The issue reports the suite passes (37 passed) with only this file restored to LF, so these files need no rule. No follow-up issue is filed.

Effort: low
Changelog: none

Fixes #3628

title: fix(app): refuse a tool wider than its slot at the command
body:
## What changed

- `camcraft_motion::machining2d::slot_centre_band` (new file `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_band.rs`) holds the slot fit rule: `h = width / 2 - r - leave`, and `h = 0` is permitted. The slot generator (`slots.rs`) and the commands call it. There is no second copy of the rule.
- `slot_gate` (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/gates.rs`) is separate from `tool_gate`. It takes the setup and the source. It runs in these commands:
  - `CreateOperation`;
  - `EditOperationLinks` (MCP `set_tool`, the UI links edit), only when the tool changes;
  - `ChangeOperationKind`.
- The gate refuses a plain Slot whose tool is too wide. The UI shows the same text after its `links not updated: ` prefix.
- The default width. `operation::seed_slot_for_tool` (`crates/app/src/operation/slot_pick.rs`) sets the width of a new Slot from the seed to the larger of 4 mm and the tool diameter. It runs at three doors:
  - the ribbon quick-add (`crates/ui/src/actions.rs`, beside `seed_helix_for_tool`);
  - MCP `add_operation`, before the params patch (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs`);
  - the change of kind (`ChangeOperationKind`, after `retype_params`).
- A tool of 4 mm or less gives the same operation as before. A width that the caller or the picks state is not changed, and the gate judges it.
- Picks that seed no slot. If `slot_from_picks` is `None`, the width is only the seed fallback. `operation::slot_width_is_stated` is then false, and the gate does not judge the width. Generate keeps its pick refusal (for example "is not a slot outline").
- `ChangeTool` (the second door, MCP `tool_edit`) refuses a diameter edit that makes the tool too wide for a plain Slot that uses it (`operation::tool_gate::resize_refusal`). It checks only when the diameter increases, and it skips operations whose picks seed no slot.
- The text is in `operation::tool_gate::slot_fit_refusal`. It uses the document unit (`units::len`) and has no G-code words.
- The generator keeps its own refusal. A project file from an older build can still hold the bad pair.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3475-tool-fit-at-edit.md`.

## The refusal text

Before: `CreateOperation` and `set_tool` accepted the tool. Generate refused later with "slot is narrower than the tool: the slot is 3.000 mm wide (0.000 mm left on each wall) and the tool is 4.000 mm".

After, at the command:

```
invalid parameters: the tool 'EM-WIDE' is 10 mm wide and the slot is 6 mm wide: choose a tool of 6 mm or less
invalid parameters: the tool 'EM-SIX' is 6 mm wide and the slot is 6 mm wide with 0.5 mm left on each wall: choose a tool of 5 mm or less
invalid parameters: S1 uses it: the tool 'EM-0400-2FL' is 100 mm wide and the slot is 6 mm wide: choose a tool of 6 mm or less
```

MCP adds its usual `set_tool: ` prefix. In an inch document the sizes are in inches.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `machining2d::slot_band::tests` (5 tests): fits, equal width, too wide, stock to leave makes it too wide, NaN / infinite / zero / negative refused cleanly.
- `camcraft-app` `--test slot_tool_fit` (new file, 7 tests):
  - `a_wide_tool_on_a_slot_is_refused_at_set_tool_and_changes_nothing` (the tool and the undo stack do not change);
  - `a_tool_that_fits_is_accepted`;
  - `a_wide_tool_on_a_slot_is_refused_at_create`;
  - `stock_to_leave_is_part_of_the_fit`;
  - `the_sentence_follows_the_document_unit`;
  - `a_tool_library_edit_that_widens_a_slot_cutter_is_refused`;
  - `a_change_of_kind_to_slot_holds_the_ops_own_tool` (a 10 mm tool gives width 10; a 4 mm tool keeps 4).
- `camcraft-app` `--test mcp`, new module `mcp/slot_tool_fit.rs` (2 tests):
  - `slot_tool_fit::set_tool_refuses_a_tool_wider_than_the_slot_without_mutation` (through `Client::refused`; `get_job` is the same after the refusal; an explicit width of 4 with a 6 mm tool is refused at `add_operation`);
  - `slot_tool_fit::add_operation_seeds_the_slot_width_from_the_tool` (a 6 mm tool gives width 6; a 3 mm tool keeps 4).
- `camcraft-app` `--test slot_dxf_sketch` (5 tests), new test `picks_that_are_no_slot_keep_their_pick_refusal_under_a_wider_tool`: a 6 mm tool on a rectangle pick is accepted at create, and generate refuses with "is not a slot outline".
- UI: no UI test was added. No UI test for a refused tool assignment exists to copy. The UI calls the same commands and the same seed function as MCP.

## Changed test

`slot_dxf_sketch::picks_that_are_no_slot_are_refused_by_name`, the plain Slot on the 3 mm outline with the 4 mm tool:

- Old: `CreateOperation` is accepted. `GenerateOperation` refuses with "slot is narrower than the tool" and "3.000 mm", "4.000 mm".
- New: `CreateOperation` refuses with "is 4 mm wide and the slot is 3 mm wide: choose a tool of 3 mm or less".

The Trochoidal Slot case did not change.

## Gate (head `bdafcfc4c`, debug, `-j 6`)

- motion `--lib` 556 pass.
- app `--lib` 300; `slot_tool_fit` 7; `slot_dxf_sketch` 5; `tilt_a180` 2; `slot_extension` 5; `tilt_heights` 8; `setup_align_2d_kinds` 8; `wcs_rotation_control` 5; `pocket_recognition` 11; `tool_gate` 10; `tool_law` 5; `mcp` 29; `mcp_doc_drift` 6; `operations` 121; `golden_cl` 33; `conformance` 7; `docs_troubleshooting` 1; `example_catalog` 37; `example_catalog_adaptive` 1; `example_catalog_edge_work` 1; `first_part_programs` 2. All pass.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` 1494 pass. Each integration binary under `crates/ui/tests` passes (23 binaries, including `operations` 31, `shell` 21, `egui_app` 8).
- clippy `-D warnings`: motion `--all-targets`; app `--lib --test slot_tool_fit --test mcp --test slot_dxf_sketch`; ui `--all-targets`. All clean.

## Not run

- No heavy lane and no light lane (P3).
- The app window was not started.

## What remains (follow-up #3631)

- 2D Pocket. Its fit needs the region that the generator cuts: the containment, the stock and the part slice. The command does not have that region, and an estimate can refuse legal work. #3631 (P3, area:mcp, effort:high) holds the pocket warning.
- The command does not refuse a Slot width edit (`EditOperationParams`) below the current tool yet. #3631 holds it too.
- The MCP reply shape of `set_tool` did not change, so `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` did not change. The `camcraft-mcp` skill row for `set_tool` can name the slot width rule. That skill is a process file, and the row is owed.

Changelog: A tool wider than a plain Slot is now refused when it is assigned (create, `set_tool`, the links edit, a change of kind) or made wider in the tool library, with both sizes and the largest tool that fits; a new Slot from the default is at least as wide as its tool.

Effort: medium

Refs #3475

title: fix(motion): the plain 3D finish hop never goes below the run end
body:
## What changed

The plain hop between two runs of `emit_runs` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/march.rs`) changed:

- The hop plane is `max(retract, next run start, current run end)`. Before, the end of the current run was not in the formula.
- The move across is made at that plane only if the plane is at or above the highest facet of the model, or if `gaplink::straight_ok` (the exact sweep) clears the move. If not, the hop goes to the clearance plane.
- When the retract plane (or clearance) is at or above the model top, the hop is the same as before, move for move. No sweep runs in that case.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3627-finish-hop-height.md`. The sentence in `docs/decisions/3362-pass-start-finish3d.md` that said each link "is certified by the existing laws" has a correction.

## The three answers (on main 7c637d705, before the fix)

Fixture: a stepped pocket (top at z 10, floor at z 5), Contour, BN-0600 (r 3), retract 7.

1. Reachable: yes. No rule refuses a retract plane below the top of the part. `sane.rs` and the height resolver check only that the value is finite. MCP `edit_operation` accepts it and `generate` gives status `ok`.
2. The tool goes into the part: yes.
3. The verifier blocks the post: yes. Findings: `rapid_in_stock`, `envelope` 3.0 mm gouge, `post_gate` gouge in 171 cells (worst 3.00 mm). `held_by: ["F1"]`. Nothing passed silently, so the coordinator set the priority to P3.

## Moves of the hop

Before:
- Feed to (7.352, -7.352, 10.0) (end of the last top pass)
- Feed down to (7.352, -7.352, 7.0) (into the part)
- Rapid to (2.705, -2.705, 7.0) (through the block)

After:
- Feed to (7.352, -7.352, 10.0)
- Rapid to (2.705, -2.705, 10.0)
- Plunge to (2.705, -2.705, 5.0)

## Pins

Each new pin is red on the old `march.rs` and green with the fix (checked by a local revert of `march.rs`):
- `camcraft-motion` `finish3d_hop_height`:
  - `a_retract_below_the_high_run_never_takes_the_tool_into_the_part` (cavity, Contour, verifier clean)
  - `inside_first_on_a_convex_part_with_a_low_retract_never_digs_in` (mesa, `contour_from(.., PassStart::Inside)`, #3362)
  - `a_retract_above_the_part_hops_clean` (retract None and 15: clean, unchanged)
- `camcraft-motion` lib `finishing3d::hop_tests` (drives `emit_runs` directly):
  - `high_run_first_with_a_low_retract_never_digs_into_the_mesa`
  - `a_retract_below_a_ridge_between_the_runs_goes_over_it`
  - `a_retract_above_the_part_is_the_plain_hop` (exact old moves)
- `camcraft-app` `finish3d_hop_height` (MCP import, edit, generate, verify):
  - `a_retract_below_the_top_of_the_part_is_accepted_and_verifies_clean`
  - `the_default_hop_verifies_clean`

Note: on the mesa with `Inside`, the verifier still gives `RapidInStock` for the hops between the base passes at z 7. The verifier reads the stock as uncut up to its top (z 10). That is its own conservative law and not this hop. The test asserts that each such rapid is above the base and off the mesa, and that no other blocking finding occurs.

## Gate (final head, debug, -j 6)

- motion: `--lib` (551 ok), `finish3d`, `finish3d_gaplink`, `finish3d_holes`, `finish3d_land`, `finish3d_overhang_and_chord`, `finish3d_pass_start`, `scallop_ceiling`, `multiaxis`, `finish3d_hop_height`: all ok. `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --no-run`: ok.
- app: `--lib` (300 ok), `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `verify`, `shared_face_bodies_finish`, `finish3d_direction`, `operations`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `first_part_programs`, `finish3d_hop_height`: all ok. The goldens did not change.
- clippy `-D warnings`: motion `--all-targets` ok; app `--lib --test finish3d_hop_height` ok.

## Not run

- No heavy lane and no light lane. The issue is P3, so it gets no heavy step.
- The rings' hop (`rings.rs`) did not change. It already lifts its plane to the ring level.

Changelog: 3D Finish: a hop between passes with a retract height below the end of the pass no longer feeds the tool down into the part; it stays at the pass height when the move across is clear, else it goes to the clearance height.

Effort: high

Fixes #3627

title: feat(multiaxis): Rotary Flow kernel - flow lines between picked helical guide chains
body:
## What changed

The first slice of the Rotary Flow kind (issue #2824, part of #2804): a 4-axis cylindrical flow-line kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`, split over four files under the 400-line law.

- `rotary_flow.rs` - the public entry. `rotary_flow(chains, facets, ax, p, c)` takes the picked guide chains, the part facets, the STATED rotation axis (the #2772 seam - the axis is a parameter, never fitted here), `RotaryFlowParams` and `AxisControl`. The params carry the `Tool` itself, so the ball-nose requirement is refused by name. Clearance and retract read as ball-center radii about the axis.
- `rotary_flow_unwrap.rs` - each chain unwound to a continuous `(theta, v)` track (the radian twin of `cl::unwrap_near`), each adjacent pair aligned by the nearest whole turn, the band developed `(s = R_ref * theta, v)` with `R_ref` the chains' outermost radius, and the picked-chain ground checks (finite, distinct, on-model, off-axis).
- `rotary_flow_pass.rs` - the iso-parametric flow curves between the aligned pair, each station's ball center pushed out along its radial until the `closest_pt_tri` oracle clears every facet (march, then bisect), the curve chorded within `min(ARC_FIT_TOL, tolerance)` over the union of the two chains' arc-length knots.
- `rotary_flow_emit.rs` - tips via the pivot law (`retip`), cut poses through the lean law on the radial (`tilt`), links rebuilt radially on the retract cylinders (`rotary_links`' law: feed retract, chorded index short way round, radial plunge), the program opening on the clearance pose (M13.8).

Refusals by name: a tool that is not a ball-nose, fewer than two chains, a non-finite point, a point off the model, a point on the axis line, chains wound in opposite senses, a band with no width, a stepover or tolerance at the scallop ceiling (the finishing kinds' own law), a station the push-out cannot clear within five radii, a pass count over the 4096-pass ceiling, a clearance that does not clear the work.

The decisions taken unattended are in `docs/decisions/2824-rotary-flow-kernel.md`: the `Tool`-carrying params (the drilling precedent), the ball-center radius reading of the heights, `R_ref` at the chains' outermost radius (ground inside it gets finer, never coarser), and one band per adjacent chain pair with both edge passes kept (a shared middle chain is walked once per band - the re-cut is the same geometry at the same depth).

## The readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 29 steps, 0 failed - motion lib, `multiaxis`, `rotary`, the new `rotary_flow` binary, and the reached app suites (operations, posed_contact, rotary_fixtures, rotary_verify, and the rest). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the rotor groove fixture: the developed band reads 4.000 mm at R 8.000 mm; 6 flow passes at a 0.9 mm stepover; the first pass rides the wall push-out (rho about 11), interior passes ride the floor a ball radius off it; every cut station's ball keeps its radius off the part.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow/rotary_flow_tests.rs` (15 tests): every refusal by name (non-ball tool, chain count, empty model, off-model at its spot, on-axis, degenerate band, opposite senses, both scallop ceilings, low clearance), the pass count law, `align_pair`'s nearest whole turn, `lerp_at`, `unwrap_near`, and a small on-model band that poses, clears and opens at clearance.
- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_flow.rs` (3 run, 1 heavy): `a_rotor_floor_band_flows_multi_turn_without_gouge` (the no-gouge pin over every station against `camcraft_sim`'s own `dist_seg_tri`, multi-turn span, wall vs floor riders), `a_pair_straddling_the_branch_aligns_by_a_whole_turn` (same pass count as the unshifted band, the note stating the shift), `climb_reverses_each_pass`, and the ignored `the_rotor_envelope_stays_gouge_free_at_the_scallop_law` (heavy lane: release --ignored, the 4-turn fine rotor envelope scanned station by station).

## What was not exercised

- The app layer, the command and the MCP tool are owed to the #2804 sub-issues; this PR changes only the motion kernel.
- The whole-turn alignment is pinned by the kernel basis' own branch (e1 = +Y on a Z axis); a pair straddling a different frame's branch reaches the same law through the same shift.
- A band whose pair meets at a whole-turn boundary exactly (offset = half a lap) is not tested; the nearest-turn law would pick either side.
- `graphify update` did not run: the `graphify` command is not on this session's PATH.
- Heavy lane: only the ignored envelope scan touches it; it runs at the cut.

Changelog: multiaxis: Rotary Flow - a 4-axis flow-line finishing kernel between picked helical guide chains on a stated rotation axis

fork synced at v0.25.0

Part of #2804. `Refs #2824`, not `Fixes`: the umbrella issue's Done means spans all its sub-issues, so the sub-issue closes with its siblings, not here.

title: fix(3d): Pass starts at on 3D Finish (Contour and Flat)
body:
## What changed

- 3D Finish gets the shared field `pass_start` (`machining2d::PassStart`, #3316) in `OpParams::Finish3D`. There is no new type.
- Project file: the shared key `pass_start` with the 3D Pocket serde attributes. Absent is Auto. `auto` is never written. There is no version step.
- Digest: `digest::write_pass_start` writes the value only off Auto, and only for Contour and Flat. Every other op keeps its stamp.
- Engine: new doors `finishing3d::contour_from(facets, p, start)` and `finishing3d::flat_from(facets, p, start)`. `contour` and `flat` keep their signatures and call the new doors with Auto. `Finish3DParams` does not change (the `direction_angle` pattern of #3426).
- `shadow_pass` collects the runs of each offset pass. For Inside it reverses the sequence of the passes. Inside one pass the loop order does not change. No loop is added or removed. Project passes Auto.
- `finishing3d::reads_pass_start(pattern)` is true only for Contour and Flat.
- Page: the shared row `Pass starts at` on the 3D Finish Passes tab. For each other pattern a line under the row names the pattern: "Not used with <pattern>: this pattern has no inside or outside ring order. Only Contour and Flat use it".
- MCP: the generic `edit_operation` (no kind-specific code).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3362-pass-start-finish3d.md`.
- Follow-up: #3624 "Pass starts at: Geodesic start side" (Geodesic shows the "Not used" line in this PR).

## Hand trace of one level (Contour)

Fixture: a 20 x 20 x 10 mm block, a ball of radius 3, a stepover of 3 mm. The top face gives four offset passes. Each pass is one square loop. Half-widths from the block centre: P0 = 10, P1 = 7, P2 = 4, P3 = 1. T is the ring tail on the flanks (`rings_and_tail`).

| Value | Cut order |
|---|---|
| Auto | P0, P1, P2, P3, T |
| Outside | P0, P1, P2, P3, T (the same moves as Auto) |
| Inside | P3, P2, P1, P0, T |

Each run goes through the existing `emit_runs` link law: a vertical hop to retract or clearance; `diagonal_ok` when `ramp` is on; `straight_ok` when the gap link is Straight. The ring tail keeps its own laws. No new link type is used.

## Readings

- Inside and Auto have the same multiset of cutting moves (338 in Contour). The only move that differs is the rise out of the last loop before the ring tail. That rise starts at the end of the last loop, so it follows the order.
- The verifier finds no blocking warning (`Warning::blocks_post`) for Auto, Inside and Outside, on Contour and on Flat (app test).
- No sideways rapid at or below the top face for any value (motion test).
- The seven Finish3D goldens in `golden_cl` do not move (`golden_cl` 33/33, no file in `crates/app/tests/golden/` changed).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_pass_start.rs`:
  - `inside_cuts_the_innermost_offset_pass_first_on_contour_and_flat`. It was red first, with the reverse disabled: `Contour: Inside cuts inside-out: [1000, 700, 400, 100, 1000]`.
  - `auto_is_the_old_contour_and_flat_move_for_move`
  - `only_the_nested_loop_patterns_read_pass_start`
- `crates/app/tests/finish3d_pass_start.rs`:
  - `the_generate_arm_hands_pass_start_to_contour_and_flat` (generate and verifier)
  - `other_patterns_keep_their_paths_and_stamp_with_a_saved_pass_start`
  - `finish3d_pass_start_rides_the_project_file`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp/finish3d_pass_start.rs`: `finish3d_pass_start_uses_mcp_history_and_never_writes_auto` (in the `mcp` binary)
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/pass_start.rs`: `the_finish3d_passes_tab_offers_pass_start_and_names_the_unused_patterns`. The Finish3D Passes list in `tests.rs` now has "Pass starts at".

## Gate (debug, by name, `-j 6`)

- motion: `--no-run` for all test binaries OK. `--lib` 548 ok. `finish3d` 55 ok (33 ignored). `finish3d_gaplink` 7, `finish3d_holes` 5, `finish3d_land` 7, `finish3d_overhang_and_chord` 3, `scallop_ceiling` 4, `multiaxis` 7, `pocket3d_pass_start` 2, `pass_start_levels` 7, `finish3d_pass_start` 3. All pass.
- app: `--lib` 299. `golden_cl` 33. `conformance` 7. `project_roundtrip` 80. `operations` 121. `mcp` 27. `mcp_doc_drift` 6. `finish3d_direction` 4. `area_controls` 13. `verify` 21. `shared_face_bodies_finish` 2. `docs_troubleshooting` 1. `example_catalog` 37, `example_catalog_adaptive` 1, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1. `first_part_programs` 2. `import_step_q02_mold` 1. `setup_align_3d` 6. `wcs_start` 6. `finish3d_pass_start` 3. title: fix(2d): name the pass start in its fallback warning, not Adaptive
body:
## Cause
The completeness guard of "Pass starts at" writes a note with `RINGS_FALLBACK`. The op counts that note and posts `Warning::StrategyFallback`. That warning had one fixed text, for the Adaptive plan. A 2D Offset, a 2D Pocket and a 3D pocket (since #3618) reach the guard. These ops do not use Adaptive, but the user saw "Adaptive fell back to Offset rings".

## Change
- `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`: new enum `FallbackCause` (`Adaptive` | `PassStart`). `StrategyFallback` gets `cause` with `#[serde(default)]`. The default is `Adaptive`. Display has one text for each cause.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs`: new constant `PASS_START_FALLBACK_TAIL` = `"this area in the Auto order instead"`. `StartSide::fallback_note` ends with it. New `pass_start_fallbacks(notes)` counts a note when it contains `PASS_START_NOTE`, contains `RINGS_FALLBACK` + the tail, and ends with the tail. The match does not read the start of the note, because 3D pocket writes the note as `Z <level>: <note>` (`machining3d/level_side.rs:62-63`). No Adaptive note ends with the tail. `rings_fallbacks` counts the two kinds as before.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: new `pub fn strategy_fallback(&Toolpath) -> Option<Warning>`. The run uses it. The cause comes from the notes, not from the op kind. `PassStart` is set only when each fallback note is a guard note. An Adaptive op on its ring fallback can write an Adaptive note and a guard note, and then the Adaptive cause stays.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`: no DTO change. The MCP kind stays `strategy_fallback`. The finding DTO is flat and has no field for the cause. The `message` carries the new text.
- `crates/ui/src/operations.rs`: the test literal gets the new field.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3542-pass-start-fallback-text.md`.
- A merge of `origin/main` (conflict in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`: the two `pub use` lines are kept).

## Texts
Old (and unchanged for the Adaptive cause):
`Adaptive fell back to Offset rings on 1 area from move 0: the notes name each one and why (the post is not held: the rings are verified)`

New (pass-start cause):
`Pass starts at: the selected start side would leave material uncut in 1 area, so the Auto order was used there instead, from move 0: the notes name each one (the post is not held: the cut is verified)`

## Pins
- `offset_pass_start::the_offset_guard_fallback_warning_names_the_pass_start`: exact text of the pass-start case from the 2D Offset guard note. The 3D pocket form (`Z 1.000: <note>`) gives the same warning. A path with an Adaptive note and a guard note keeps the Adaptive cause.
- `offset_pass_start::a_strategy_fallback_saved_without_a_cause_reads_as_adaptive`: a cache without `cause` reads as `Adaptive`. The serde name `strategy_fallback` does not change. The round trip of `pass_start` is exact.
- `strategy_fallback::an_adaptive_fallback_to_offset_rings_is_a_warning`: an exact `assert_eq!` of the Adaptive text from a real generation (proves "unchanged").
- `mcp::job::tests::a_pass_start_fallback_keeps_the_strategy_fallback_kind` (app lib): the kind is `strategy_fallback` and advisory for the two causes.
- `machining2d::pass_start::tests::the_guard_fallback_is_an_offset_rings_fallback` (motion lib): `pass_start_fallbacks` counts the guard note and the `Z 1.000: ` prefixed note. It does not count the two Adaptive note forms. `rings_fallbacks` counts each of them one time.

## Gate (head f9f9cf385, debug, `-j 6`)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: all binaries pass.
- motion `--lib` 548; `pass_start_levels` 7; `pocket3d_pass_start` 2. All pass.
- app `--lib` 300; `strategy_fallback` 1; `offset_pass_start` 6 (2 ignored heavy); `pocket_pass_start` 6; `adaptive_pass_start` 4; `adaptive_zero_margin_island` 4; `pocket3d_pass_start` 3; `docs_troubleshooting` 1; `mcp_verify` 3; `golden_cl` 33; `conformance` 7; `example_catalog` 37 (4 ignored); `first_part_programs` 2. All pass.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` 1493 pass.
- clippy `-D warnings`: sim and motion `--all-targets`, app `--lib` + `offset_pass_start` + `strategy_fallback`, ui `--all-targets`. Clean.

## Not run
- No heavy lane (P3). No app window.
- The red-first run of the new Offset text was not shown separately. Before this change the only text was the Adaptive text, so the `assert_eq!` cannot pass on the old code.
- No fixture hits the guard on a real op. `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_pass_start.rs` has no case that falls back. The tests feed the real guard note (`StartSide::fallback_note`, also in its 3D pocket form) to the same function that the run uses.

## Follow-up
- #3622 (P7): the area count is not true for 3D pocket levels (one note for each level) and for an Adaptive ring fallback with a guard fallback (two notes for one area). This is the "Also seen" item of the issue.

Changelog: The warning after a "Pass starts at" fallback (2D Offset, 2D Pocket, 3D pocket) now names the pass start and the Auto order, not the Adaptive strategy.

Effort: medium

Fixes #3542

title: perf(sim): sample verifier island planes at cut levels
body:
<!-- HELD DRAFT: do not merge. The equivalence proof failed. -->

**Status: HELD. The equivalence proof failed, so this change does not merge.**

## What changed

Law (c) (`band_reach_counted`) builds the model planes for its island boundary samples from the cut LEVELS plus the deepest cut. The builder is `crates/sim/src/verify/cut_planes.rs`. `Rest::new` is unchanged and still keys a cut per feed chord. No other law changes.

Files:
- `crates/sim/src/verify/cut_planes.rs` (new)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs` (call site)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/rest.rs` (`cut()` accessor is test-only now)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/reach_tests.rs` (cost assertion; verdict pin unchanged)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/mod.rs`, `docs/decisions/3615-verify-cut-levels.md`

## The equivalence result (the gate is RED)

The pin `verify::reach_tests::a_many_plane_ramp_reads_only_the_samples_near_its_discs` fails on the existing sloped ramp fixture `ramp_at(500, 36.0)`.

- All-plane reference (`reach_reference`): `ShankHit { part: true }` at moves 250 to 292 and 293 to 329.
- New levels plus deepest: `ShankHit { part: true }` at moves 250 to 273 and 293 to 329.
- Lost: moves 274 to 292. That is 19 part-true convictions.

The lost moves are real collisions. The shank bottom stands below the boss top Z 10 and its rim reaches 1 mm into the boss wall. The flute did not clear that wall point. The per-chord planes also place triangulation-tie wall vertices at z-dependent positions, and those points catch the moves. One plane cannot reproduce them.

The other pins pass: `indexed_band_reach_keeps_every_finding_of_the_pooled_scan`, `degenerate_paths_match_the_pooled_scan_and_do_not_panic`, and the three `cut_planes` unit tests.

## Readings

- Away-from-wall ramp `ramp_at(2000, 34)` where verdicts do match: new `slices = 1`, `sample_tests = 0`; old `slices = 2000`, `sample_tests = 32,016,000`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: NOT RUN. Condition 4 says STOP when any verdict differs. A heavy lane cannot recover a lost verdict, so the proof stopped at the pin.

## What was not exercised

- The full heavy sim/verify lanes and the release tier.
- The real #3577 fig8 path. The counterexample is the existing sloped ramp fixture, and it is enough to stop.

## Why this is held

A verifier change that loses part-true collisions is less conservative. The Prime Directive forbids it. A fix needs a plane set that keeps this wall coverage while it collapses the duplicate planes, for example a bounded set of wall points or samples taken from the mesh edges. That is a new design, not the levels-plus-deepest set.

`docs/decisions/3615-verify-cut-levels.md` has the full record.

title: fix(3d): Pass starts at on 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

3D Pocket gets the shared parameter "Pass starts at" (Auto / Inside / Outside) of #3316. It uses the same type, key, row and MCP door as 2D Offset.

- `OpParams::Pocket3D` and the engine's `Pocket3DParams` get the field `pass_start: machining2d::PassStart`. The engine field has a doc line that keeps room for the start and exit points of #1448. There is no code for them.
- Project file: the key `pass_start` (`PassStartDto`). The file does not write `auto`. A file without the key reads Auto. There is no version step.
- Digest: `digest::write_pass_start` writes the value only off Auto. Each earlier operation keeps its cache stamp.
- Planner (`crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_side.rs`, new, and `hsm.rs`): Waterline and Offset rings call the 2D ring law through the new door `machining2d::level_ring_plan` (`level_rings.rs`). The door uses the same `level_pieces`, `order` and completeness guard as 2D Offset. The 3D level's cutter-centre area is its own outline, so the start side is read off the edges of `center` (offset 0). The 2D `ring_plan` keeps its arguments and its output.
- Auto: the same `plan_passes` call as before. No Auto move can change.
- Zigzag, and Auto (which cuts rows): no ring order. The moves do not change. The path says `PASS_START_ZIGZAG_NOTE` once. The Adaptive HSM spiral: no ring order, `PASS_START_ADAPTIVE_NOTE` once. The rest pass: `PASS_START_REST_NOTE` once. The rotary wrap keeps Auto. Rotary Offset and Multi-Axis Rough always send Auto.
- UI: the shared row `Pass starts at` on the 3D Pocket Passes tab. If the strategy is not Waterline or Offset rings, a line under the row says that the value is not used (`POCKET3D_NO_RING_ORDER`).
- MCP: no new code. The generic `edit_operation` carries the key.
- 30 motion test files and 17 app/ui test files get one line `pass_start: Default::default()` in their struct literals (no other change).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3361-pass-start-pocket3d.md`.

## Hand trace of one level

Fixture of `pocket3d_pass_start` (motion): a 40 mm square pocket, a 10 mm square island in the middle, tool radius 3, Waterline, stepover 2.4, one level at Z 0. The cutter-centre band runs from the island ring (Chebyshev distance 8 from the island centre, 7.1 at the round corners) to the wall ring (17). The numbers are the Chebyshev distance of each ring, in cut order.

- Auto: 12.2 -> 14.6 -> 17.0, then 12.2, then 10.4 -> 8.8, then the island ring 8.0 last. This is the core-first order of today.
- Inside: island ring 8.0 first -> 10.4 -> 12.8 -> 15.2 -> the wall ring 17 last. The path says the island wall note.
- Outside: the wall ring 17.0 first -> 14.6 -> 12.2 -> 9.8 -> 7.4 (clipped pieces) -> the island ring last. The path says the outer wall note.

No completeness fallback on any value. Each cut stays in the band.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pocket3d_pass_start`:
  - `inside_and_outside_force_the_ring_order_of_a_3d_level` (Waterline and Offset rings). The test was red first: with the side forced to Auto, it failed with "Waterline: Inside starts on the island ring, at 12.2".
  - `zigzag_keeps_its_rows_and_names_the_unused_choice` (Zigzag and Auto: the same moves, the note once).
- `camcraft-app` `pocket3d_pass_start`:
  - `the_generate_arm_hands_pass_start_to_the_3d_ladder` (40 mm block in its stock, Waterline, the first cut of each value, no added verify warning).
  - `pocket3d_pass_start_rides_the_project_file` (key absent for Auto, present for Inside and Outside, a file without the key reads Auto, an unknown word is refused).
  - `mcp_sets_pocket3d_pass_start_and_undo_redo_walk_it` (`edit_operation`, undo, redo).
- `camcraft-app` lib: `pass_start_moves_the_pocket3d_stamp_only_off_auto`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `the_pocket3d_passes_tab_offers_pass_start_and_names_the_row_strategies`, and the 3D Pocket row of `every_field_lives_on_exactly_one_section`.

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- Skims on an open run are not judged per pass by the wire verify (it
  refuses them by name); a follow-up can split the passes and judge
  each at its own kerf.
- Taper, burnout and 4-axis cuts do not read the overlap; each refuses
  an open run or walks the closed lap as before.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

Changelog: Wire Contour: a stated closing overlap rides the cut past its seam; a centre-line slit side for open runs; skim passes on open runs re-entered from the air.

title: feat: open a project read-only with --read-only and open_project read_only
body:
## What changed

`camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens a project read-only. The MCP
tool `open_project` takes `read_only: true` for the same result. A save
over the opened file is then refused on every save route, and the file
stays byte for byte. A save to another file works and ends read-only. The
title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.

- One rule, `project::refuse_read_only_save` in `crates/app/src/project/`,
  refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The
  window's `State::save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it.
  `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP
  seam of a window.
- The rule compares canonical paths, so a save from the Save As dialog
  to the opened file is refused too.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as
  the editor for shipped machines does. The Save of the unsaved-changes
  prompt does the same.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- The read-only state is kept next to the document path:
  `State::project_read_only` in the window, `Env::doc_read_only` in a
  headless MCP session or a script run. The live seam gets the window's
  state through `LiveOptions::read_only`.
- A model file with `--read-only` is imported as usual. A headless start
  ignores the option. The live seam still refuses `open_project`.
- The same option name and behaviour as the open SolidCraft proposal
  for `--read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830).
- No change to the file format or `PROJECT_VERSION`.
- Docs: the `--help` text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`,
  `site/content/guide/automate/cli.md` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3609-read-only-open.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`.

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/read_only_open.rs`:

- `the_rule_refuses_only_the_opened_file_of_a_read_only_project`
- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_keeps_it`
- `a_save_to_another_file_works_and_ends_read_only`
- `a_plain_open_ends_read_only_and_a_bad_flag_changes_nothing`
- `a_script_save_after_a_read_only_open_is_refused`
- `the_live_seam_refuses_an_approved_save_over_a_read_only_window_project`

New in `crates/ui/src/launch_file_tests.rs`:

- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_save_as_ends_read_only`
- `read_only_changes_nothing_for_a_model_file`

New in `crates/ui/src/cli_options_tests.rs`:

- `read_only_is_a_switch_that_keeps_the_file_after_it`

`cargo xtask gate quick` (Windows 11, on `60b19abe8` plus this change):
214 of 216 steps passed. The two red steps are not from this change:

- `example_catalog`: `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::{rebuilds,regenerates}`.
  The refusal text is equal, and only the line end is different. The
  checkout uses `core.autocrlf=true`, so `refusal.txt` has `\r\n`.
- `first_part_programs`: `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`.
  It also fails on `60b19abe8` (#3574).

The steps of this change all passed:

- `read_only_open`: 6 passed.
- `mcp_live`: 14 passed.
- `mcp_doc_drift`: 6 passed.
- `mcp`: 24 passed.
- `scripting`: 20 passed.
- The app lib tests: 298 passed.
- The `camcraft-ui` lib tests: 1476 passed, 8 ignored. These include
  `launch_file_tests` and `cli_options_tests`.
- The 16 ui suites, among them `gpu_render`, `shell` and `operations`.

The other app steps are the suites that the gate maps from
`app::project`, `app::script` and `app::mcp`.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
The gate and clippy ran on this change before the issue existed. The head
differs from that tree only in the issue number: in code comments and in

Heavy lanes: not run (no heavy step for a `P2` or lower PR, #3556).
Reach from `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run`: every `app` heavy target

## Not in this change

- A read-only open on the live seam. The live seam refuses

  unsaved-changes prompt. The window's read-only state still reaches a
  live `save_project`.
- A new script form `cam.load(path, options)`. Scripts use
  `cam.call("open_project", {path, read_only: true})`.
- `read_only` in `get_job`.
- The window does not follow the path of a live `save_project` with a
  new path. This is the behaviour today. The window keeps its path and
  stays read-only.
- A reopen from the recent list, or in a later session, is not
  read-only. The recent list keeps paths only.
- The read-only bit of the file on disk.
- A hand-off of the flag to a running window. CamCraft has no
  single-instance hand-off.

- The live seam through a real window and the AI chat's Allow prompt.
  A test calls `answer_live_with` with the options that the window builds.
- Linux and macOS.
- A project on a network share.

title: fix(project): ask or refuse before a save writes over a changed project file
body:
## What changed

A save to the project's own file now checks the file on disk first. The
project remembers the file's disk stamp (path, size, modification time)
when it is opened and after each save. If the stamp is different at the
next save, the file on disk changed after the open or the last save:

- The window holds the save and asks: **Save As**, **Cancel** or
  **Overwrite**. Nothing is written before the answer.
- `cam.save` and the MCP tool `save_project` refuse by name. The refusal
  names the file and `overwrite: true`. `save_project` has a new optional
  argument `overwrite`. `cam.save` has a new options object:
  `cam.save(path?, { overwrite?: boolean })`.
- An agent attached to the window uses the window's stamp. The live seam
  takes it in (`LiveOptions::doc_stamp`) and gives the new stamp back
  (`LiveAnswer::doc_stamp`), so the window does not ask about the
  agent's own save.

A save to another path, a new document and a file that was deleted are
not checked. The stamp of our own save replaces the old stamp, so the
next save does not ask. In the window, New and Open drop the old stamp
and a held save, so a held save never writes another document.

- The stamp is `project::DiskStamp`, beside `project::save` and
  `project::load`. The checks are `script::save_guard::check` and
  `State::may_save_over`.
  `project::save`, the file format and `PROJECT_VERSION` do not change.
- Behaviour change: a script or an agent that saved over a changed file
  is now refused. It must pass `overwrite: true`.
- The behaviour matches SolidCraft's overwrite guard. The texts are
  CamCraft's own.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are updated for
  the new argument. The MCP and CLI guide pages have one paragraph each.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3608-save-overwrite-guard.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`.

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/save_overwrite_guard.rs`:

- `a_stamp_sees_a_foreign_write_but_not_a_missing_file_or_another_path`
- `an_mcp_save_over_a_changed_file_is_refused_until_overwrite`
- `an_mcp_open_stamps_the_file`
- `a_save_to_another_path_or_over_a_deleted_file_is_not_refused`
- `a_bad_save_option_is_refused_by_name_and_writes_nothing`
- `a_script_save_over_a_changed_file_is_refused_until_overwrite`
- `an_attached_agent_save_meets_the_window_stamp_and_hands_back_the_new_one`

New in `crates/ui/src/save_guard_tests.rs`:

- `a_save_over_a_changed_file_asks_and_overwrite_replaces_it`
- `cancel_keeps_the_file_and_save_as_goes_to_the_save_as_dialog`
- `the_window_s_own_saves_never_ask`
- `a_save_to_another_file_or_over_a_deleted_file_does_not_ask`
- `a_held_save_from_the_unsaved_prompt_keeps_the_document_open`
- `a_new_document_drops_a_held_save`

New layout test: `layout_window_overwrite_prompt`
(`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/page_layout_windows.rs`).

`cargo xtask gate quick` (Windows 11): 216 steps, 214 passed, 2 failed,
0 stalled. It ran the app and ui libs (ui lib: 1480 passed, the new tests
and the layout test among them), `save_overwrite_guard` (7 passed),
`mcp_live`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `scripting`, every app suite that names
`app::project`, `app::script` or `mcp (tools)`, and 16 ui suites.
The 2 failed steps do not touch this change:

- `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`
  fails on upstream/main `60b19abe8` (#3574, main is red).
- `example_catalog::catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::{rebuilds,regenerates}`
  differs only by line ends: this Windows checkout (`core.autocrlf=true`)
  turns the LF file `examples/catalog/2d/drill-overfeed/refusal.txt`
  into CRLF.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
The gate and clippy ran on this change before the issue existed. The head
differs from that tree only in the issue number: in code comments and in
the name of the decision file.
Heavy lanes: not run. The change is not under the safety floor (no
posted G-code, collision check, simulation or geometry), so no targeted
heavy step applies (#3556).
Reach from `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run`: "app heavy: every target"
(212 steps), because `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs` changed. Not run.

## Not exercised

- The window's step that keeps an agent's new stamp (`mcp_host.rs`, three
  lines). The app test pins the stamp that the live seam gives back. The
  AI chat's Allow path is not driven in a test.
- The prompt's buttons by a click. The tests call
  `actions::resolve_overwrite`, and the layout test checks the modal.
- Save As after the prompt: it opens the system file dialog. The test
  checks that the Save As command is queued.
- A write that keeps the size and the modification time. Some file systems
  keep the time in steps of 1 or 2 seconds. This is a known limit.
- Two real CamCraft processes, git, a sync client and a network share. A
  plain write of other bytes stands in for each.
- Linux and macOS.
