title: test(ui): GPU lib tests take one process-wide lock
body:
## What changed

The `camcraft-ui` lib tests that make a wgpu instance now use the GPU one at a time. The change is in test code only.

- New test-only module `crates/ui/src/egui_app/gpu_test_lock.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`). It holds one process-wide `Mutex<()>` and the function `gpu_guard()`.
- The lock is poison-tolerant. A test that panics with the lock held does not make the other GPU tests fail.
- A holder counter fails a test if two tests hold the lock at the same time.
- Eight tests take the guard as their first statement:
  - `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`
  - `egui_app::gpu::tests::adapter_probe_names_the_gpu`
  - six `egui_app::report_tests` tests that push a kind button. The screenshot request makes `egui_kittest` start its wgpu renderer in `step()`.
- The guard comes before the harness. Thus the harness and its renderer drop first, and the lock is released last.
- The context pack named seven tests. `the_door_opens_the_window_and_a_kind_button_files_the_url` also pushes a kind button ("Request a feature"), so it takes the lock too.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3589-gpu-test-lock.md`. A shared instance was dropped: kittest makes its own device, and the headless run makes its device through `camcraft_gpu::device()`.

## Product path

The product does not make two wgpu instances or devices at the same time. This is from a read of the code (scout pack on main 60376ccbb), not from a run:

- The desktop app makes one instance, one adapter and one device on the UI thread (`gpu_init.rs`). It tries the backends in sequence. It drops each failed attempt before the next one.
- The `--headless` run makes one instance on the calling thread (`crates/gpu/src/adapter.rs`).
- `shared_device()` and `cut_or_cpu` have no caller outside `camcraft-gpu`.
- No worker thread touches a device.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::gpu_test_lock::every_gpu_test_takes_the_lock`: reads the source of the eight tests. It requires `let _gpu = gpu_guard()` as the first statement of each.
- `egui_app::gpu_test_lock::the_lock_lets_one_holder_in_at_a_time`: 8 threads take the lock 20 times each. The counter must never be more than 1.
- `egui_app::gpu_test_lock::a_panic_with_the_lock_held_does_not_block_the_next_test`

A test cannot prove that a random driver crash does not occur again. The proof is the repeat runs of the reporter on the affected machine.

## Readings (this machine, Windows 11, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -j 6`)

- Run 1: ok. 1484 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored (88.66 s). No 0xc0000005.
- Run 2: ok. 1484 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored (88.88 s). No 0xc0000005.
- Run 3: ok. 1484 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored (89.94 s). No 0xc0000005.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean. The only warning is the old manifest warning about the unused workspace dependency `truck-polymesh`.
- The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes up by 3. There is no snapshot PNG change and no new dependency.

## Not exercised

- This machine did not show the crash before the change. The 20 runs on the reporter's machine are the test.
- No heavy lane was run: this is a P2 PR with test code only.
- The integration test binaries of `crates/ui` (`gpu_render`, `trace_*`, `catalog_render`) are separate processes and are not changed.

title: test(app): expect the creation order after undo of delete_setup
body:
## Cause

PR #3485 (#3447) changed the setup order of the program from the name order to the creation order. This change is on purpose. The MCP test `move_an_operation_delete_the_emptied_setup_and_undo_redo_both` in `crates/app/tests/mcp_setup_moves.rs` still asserted the old name order after the undo of `delete_setup`. The test creates "Front" first and "Back" second, so the correct order is `["Front","Back"]`. The post-merge run 45093122162 on edcbfe4dd failed on this assert.

The product is correct. `setup_delete_order` (added by #3485) pins the product undo: undo of `DeleteSetup` puts the setup back at its old place, and the posted program does not change.

## Change (test only)

- Old: after `undo`, `assert_eq!(c.shape().0, vec!["Back", "Front"])` (name order).
- New: before the delete, the test captures the setup list and asserts `["Front","Back"]` (creation order). After `undo`, it asserts that the list is equal to the captured list.
- New: after `redo` and the next `undo`, the test asserts the captured list again. The old test did not assert the list at this point.

No undo or redo assert is weaker. No product code changes. No post output changes. `PROJECT_VERSION` stays 77.

## Readings and pinning tests

All runs are debug, `-j 6`, by binary name, on head 1c6002baa:

- `mcp_setup_moves`: 3 passed (the failing test is green).
- Each `crates/app/tests/mcp*.rs` binary (49 binaries, `mcp` to `mcp_workholding`): all pass, 0 failed.
- `setup_creation_order`: 4 passed. `setup_delete_order`: 2 passed. `setups`: 12 passed. `project_roundtrip`: 80 passed.
- `camcraft-app --lib`: 298 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test mcp_setup_moves -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not run

- The other app test binaries, the UI suites, the light lane and the heavy lanes. The diff changes one test file only.

title: fix(verify): name a cut deeper than the flute length first
body:
## What changed

A 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset or 2D Contour can cut deeper below the stock top than the flute length of its tool. The operation now gives that cause first.

- **Always a note, first in the notes.** It has the tool name. Text for the #3319 case:
  `EM-0800-4FL has a flute length of 10.000 mm; this operation cuts 20.500 mm below the stock top; above the flutes, the shank or the holder goes into the cut and can rub or collide - use a tool with a flute length of at least 20.500 mm, or cut less deep`
- **A warning `flute_short`, first in the warning list.** It comes only when the shank or holder laws convict the body on the same path (`ShankHit`, `HolderHit`, `SweepHit`). Text:
  `the tool's flute length is 10.000 mm, but the cut goes 20.500 mm below the stock top from move N: above the flutes, the shank or the holder goes into the cut; the findings after this one name the moves where it meets material - use a tool with a longer flute, or cut less deep (this finding alone does not hold the post)`
- **Advisory, never a block.** `blocks_post()` is false. The shank and holder findings hold the post, as before. The #3319 case stays blocked by its shank findings.
- No verifier law, collision check or rapid check changes. The text of `RapidInStock` does not change (that is #3520).

Where:
- The law: `crates/sim/src/verify/flute_reach.rs` (`flute_reach`, `flute_note`). It compares the lowest cutting tip with the stock top.
- The new kind and its text: `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs` (`Warning::FluteShort`).
- The placement: `crates/app/src/operation/flute_law.rs` (`name_first`), called at the end of the upright arm in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`.
- The MCP kind name `flute_short`: `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs`. The located move: `crates/app/src/warned_moves.rs`. The folded UI line: `crates/ui/src/operations.rs`.
- The decision: `docs/decisions/3525-flute-reach-law.md`.

Why a warning only beside a body finding: the first form blocked the post for a wider shank. `tool_body_beside_shank::t31_verify_judges_shank_at_6_35_below_38_1_and_catches_real_holder_hit` disproved it: that 2D Contour cuts 25 mm with a 14.478 mm flute and verifies clean. `t31` asserts that the clean program has no finding at all, so a clean path gets the note alone. The text claims no contact and does not say that the shank is wider: the `ToolGeom` of `t31` reads a 17.5 mm shank radius (widened to its holder profile) over a 6.35 mm shank.

## Readings

- #3319 case (`fig8.step`, `EM-0800-4FL` with flute 10, Top = stock top, Bottom = selection +1.5, stepdown 10): `flute_short` first, depth 20.500 mm; then the `shank_hit` findings and the three `RapidInStock` findings of #3319; the post is refused on the shank findings.
- The same job with the catalog flute (20 mm): the same, depth 20.500 mm.
- Flute 25 mm: no note, no warning.
- Shank diameter = cutter diameter, flute 10 mm: the note first, no warning, and the program posts.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/sim/tests/flute_reach.rs` (new, 3 tests): `a_cut_past_the_flute_is_named_at_the_first_deep_move` (exact warning and note texts, first deep move, advisory), `a_flute_longer_than_the_cut_gives_no_finding`, `rapids_and_unstated_flutes_are_not_read`.
- `crates/app/tests/flute_reach.rs` (new, 4 tests):
  - `a_ten_mm_flute_names_its_cause_before_the_rapid_findings`: the #3319 case. It is `#[ignore]` heavy lane, because it takes about 65 s in debug. It passes in release.
  - `the_catalog_flute_names_its_cause_before_the_shank_findings`: a plain debug test of the same job with the 20 mm catalog flute, about 35 s. It is not a light twin: it runs in the debug suite.
  - `a_twenty_five_mm_flute_gets_no_flute_finding`.
  - `a_same_diameter_shank_past_the_flute_is_an_advisory_note`.

## Changed asserts

- `mcp_verify::verify_is_not_ok_while_an_ops_own_warnings_hold_the_post`:
  - old: every finding is `shank_hit` and holds the post;
  - new: `findings[0]` is `flute_short` with `blocks_post` false, there is more than one finding, and every finding after it is `shank_hit` and holds the post. The asserts that `ok` is false, that `held_by` is `["C1"]`, and that the post is refused stay.
- `strategy_fallback::an_adaptive_fallback_to_offset_rings_is_a_warning`: no change. That path has no body finding, so it gets the note only, and "no other warning" holds.
- `shoulder_adaptive::containment_outside_without_stock_clears_with_extension_never_the_recess`: no change. Same reason: `warns == 1` holds, and the note asserts use `any`.
- `tool_body_beside_shank::t31_verify_judges_shank_at_6_35_below_38_1_and_catches_real_holder_hit`: no change, green.

No assert is removed.

## Gate (head 274ca1483)

- Quick plan (`--base` the merge base): 390 steps. The selected subset ran: 103 steps green, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 2616 tests passed, 26 ignored. The subset is:
  - all `sim suites` steps;
  - the touched `motion` steps;
  - `ui suites: lib` (1477 passed) and `ui suites: operations`;
  - the app steps `lib`, `verify*`, `strategy_fallback`, `offset_pass_start`, `posting`, `solid_law_goldens`, `first_part_programs`, the three `example_catalog*` suites, `flute_reach`, `mcp_verify`, and each app step whose name has shank, holder, collision, rapid, warning, warned, pocket, offset, adaptive, contour or clearance.
- `gate batch --only`: `app suites: golden_cl`, `app suites: conformance`: green.
- `flute_reach` (app) in release with `--include-ignored`: 4 passed.
- clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-sim --all-targets`, `-p camcraft-app --lib --tests`, `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets`: clean.
- Light lane: not run. The dry-run lists two motion twins (`the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light`, `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light`). The motion release build is cold, and this diff does not touch motion.

What moved: no golden, no catalog program, no posted output. The pinned warning list of `mcp_verify` moved (above).

## Not exercised

- The 287 quick-plan steps outside the subset (mostly turning, wire, probe and multi-axis suites). Their kinds are not judged by the law.
- A stock with steps: the depth is read against the stock top, so a stepped stock can give a depth that is too large at one place.
- The UI fold line, seen in a window (no window was started).
- No heavy lane: P3.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket, Adaptive, Offset or Contour that cuts deeper than its tool's flute length now says so first: a note with the tool, the flute length and the depth, and an advisory `flute_short` warning before the shank or holder findings that it explains.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Refs #3319
Refs #3520
Fixes #3525

title: fix(post): name the wire post Native wire EDM job files
body:
## What changed

- The wire post "Agie native wire EDM" has the new name "Native wire EDM job files". The name is one constant, `posting::agie::POST`.
- The old name is a hidden alias. A saved project, an option key, a script, an MCP call or a machine file that uses the old name still selects the post. No list shows the old name.
- Refusals and UI texts say what is wrong with the job. They do not name the machine brand.
- The 11 `agie-native` `.refusal` goldens change with the `.cps` throw text. No posted program changes.

## User-visible names that changed

| Old text | New text | File |
|---|---|---|
| `Agie native wire EDM` (post name) | `Native wire EDM job files` | `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs` (`POST`), `assets/posts/agie-native.cps:3`, `examples/agie/punch.camscript`, `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md:148` |
| `.cps` option group `Agie technology` | `Wire EDM technology` | `assets/posts/agie-native.cps:10`, `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md` |
| `.cps` throw `Agie native wire EDM requires the desktop or CLI One program post to a new job directory` | `Native wire EDM job files require the desktop or CLI One program post to a new job directory` | `assets/posts/agie-native.cps:16` |
| Status line `Agie job prepared in {} ({} controller files, zero working steps)` | `Native wire EDM job prepared in {} (...)` | `crates/ui/src/state.rs` |
| Error `Enter an Agie job name of up to eight uppercase letters or digits, starting with a letter` | `Enter a job name of up to eight uppercase letters or digits, starting with a letter` | `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog.rs` |
| Error `Choose One program to create an Agie job directory` | `Choose One program to create a native wire EDM job directory` | `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog.rs` |
| Folder picker title `Choose a parent folder for the Agie job` | `Choose a parent folder for the native wire EDM job` | `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog.rs` |
| Label `A new job folder will contain the native Agie controller files.` | `A new job folder will contain the native controller files.` | `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog_tabs.rs` |
| Label `Check the effective work quality on Agie Control before assigning cutting steps.` | `Check the effective work quality on the control before assigning cutting steps.` | `crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog_tabs.rs` |

Refusals, grouped by file. The rule: "Agie requires X" -> "The native wire EDM job requires X"; "Agie jobs ..." -> "Native wire EDM jobs ..."; "Agie cannot verify" -> "The native wire EDM post cannot verify"; in `camcraft-post`, "Agie <noun>" -> "The <noun>" or "The job".

| File | Refusals changed | Examples (old -> new) |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs` | 19 | `The Agie job requires a Wire Contour` -> `The native wire EDM job requires a Wire Contour`; `Agie QN2 controls the dielectric settings; ...` -> `The AGIE_QN2 condition controls the dielectric settings; ...`; `Agie work extends outside the stated wire guide heights` -> `The wire work extends outside the stated wire guide heights` |
| `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs` | 12 | `The Agie job requires the {MODEL} machine profile` -> `The native wire EDM job requires the {MODEL} machine profile`; `Agie jobs require default post options and One program output` -> `Native wire EDM jobs require default post options and One program output`; `Agie post blocked - {op_name}: {text}` -> `Native wire EDM post blocked - {op_name}: {text}`; `Agie operation is unavailable` -> `The Wire Contour operation is unavailable` |
| `crates/app/src/posting.rs` | 1 | `Agie native jobs require a job directory on the desktop or CLI` -> `Native wire EDM jobs require a job directory on the desktop or CLI` |
| `crates/app/src/posting_per_op.rs` | 1 | `Choose One program to create a native Agie job directory` -> `Choose One program to create a native wire EDM job directory` |
| `crates/app/src/posting_mounts.rs` | 1 | `An Agie job requires a single mount and setup` -> `A native wire EDM job requires a single mount and setup` |
| `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs` | 15 | `Agie coordinates must be finite and within ±9999.9999 mm` -> `Job coordinates must be finite and within ±9999.9999 mm`; `Agie nominal contour crosses or touches itself` -> `The nominal contour crosses or touches itself`; `The Agie rough pass and wire need at least 0.4 mm ...` -> `The rough pass and wire need at least 0.4 mm ...` |
| `crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs` | 9 | `Set the Agie separation cut length (separationLengthMm) ...` -> `Set the separation cut length (separationLengthMm) ...`; `Agie destination {} already exists; choose a new directory` -> `Job destination {} already exists; choose a new directory`; `Agie bundle output requires a local filesystem` -> `Job bundle output requires a local filesystem` |

Total: 58 refusal lines, 6 UI strings, 3 `.cps` strings, 1 post name.

## What did not change

- Identifiers, module names, file names and test names: `posting_agie.rs`, `agie_profile.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/`, `agie-native.cps`, the `agie-native` golden folders, `examples/agie/`, `mod agie_post`. Open PRs use these names.
- `AGIECUT CLASSIC 2S` (the model in the `.mch` and in the machine-profile refusal): it is the value that the mounted machine file must state. The refusal must name it to say what to mount.
- `AGIE_QN2`: a condition ID that the operator enters on the machine.
- `AGIE.USING_` records: posted controller-file text.
- The user guide title and "Agie Control" in the user guide: they describe the machine and its control, not a feature of CamCraft.
- The script receipt value `"format": "Agie native wire EDM"` (`crates/app/src/script/report.rs`): a script can read it. A change is a breaking change (coordinator decision 4).
- `extension = "agie"` in `agie-native.cps`: an identifier of the output, not traced to a user-visible text.
- The attribution in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` and `site/static/icons/LICENSES.txt`.
- Posted output: no `.nc` golden and no controller-file golden (`CCSEP20.SBR`, `CCSEP20.SBL`, `CCSEP20.ISO`) changed. No snapshot PNG changed.

## The hidden alias

`posting::agie::LEGACY_POST` holds the old name. `current_name`, `current_ref` and `current_key` (in `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs`) change it to the new name. They run where a name comes in:

- the project file: the document post (`project/apply.rs`) and a setup's own post (`project/mount_dto.rs`);
- the option keys `builtin:<name>`: `PostScriptOptions::normalize` (`schema.rs`) moves the old key to the new key; an entry under the new key wins;
- the commands `SelectPost::new` (`commands/post.rs`) and `SetSetupPost::new` (`commands/setup_mount.rs`): GUI, MCP and script;
- `posting::resolve_cps`: the script `cam.post({cps})`, the MCP `post` tool and the CLI;
- a machine file's stated post: the `controller.post` check (`machine/validate.rs`) and the post offer (`posting_offer.rs`);
- `agie::is_native` also accepts the old name.

No list shows the old name: `BUILTINS`, `WIRE_POSTS`, the post picker and the MCP name list hold only the new name. The world stores only the new name, so a save writes the new name. The project file version does not change.

Tests (`crates/app/tests/wire_post_alias.rs`):
- `the_new_name_is_listed_and_the_old_name_is_not`
- `the_old_name_selects_the_new_post_by_command_script_and_lookup` (with undo)
- `a_project_saved_with_the_old_name_opens_posts_and_saves_the_new_name`
- `an_option_map_under_the_old_key_normalizes_to_the_new_key`

## Goldens

- 11 files in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/agie-native/`: `arcs`, `css_then_live`, `drill_retract`, `empty_section`, `extreme_coords`, `full_circle`, `full_circle_raw`, `live_then_stop`, `probe`, `rotary`, `tool_change` (`.refusal`).
- Only line 2 changed. It holds the text of the `.cps` throw at line 16, which changed with the post name. The position `user.cps:16:9` is the same.
- I changed them by a text replace of the old throw text with the new throw text, not by a regeneration.
- The golden test `script_agie_native` confirms them: `11 passed`.

## Tests and gates on head `14e01be84`

All commands run in the worktree with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`.

- `cargo xtask gate test the_new_name_is_listed_and_the_old_name_is_not --crate camcraft-app --binary wire_post_alias --exact`: `passed (4 of 4 tests in `wire_post_alias` passed)`
- `cargo xtask gate test the_old_name_selects_the_new_post_by_command_script_and_lookup --crate camcraft-app --binary wire_post_alias --exact`: `passed (4 of 4 tests in `wire_post_alias` passed)`
- `cargo xtask gate test a_project_saved_with_the_old_name_opens_posts_and_saves_the_new_name --crate camcraft-app --binary wire_post_alias --exact`: `passed (4 of 4 tests in `wire_post_alias` passed)`
- `cargo xtask gate test an_option_map_under_the_old_key_normalizes_to_the_new_key --crate camcraft-app --binary wire_post_alias --exact`: `passed (4 of 4 tests in `wire_post_alias` passed)`
- `cargo xtask gate test list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law --crate camcraft-app --binary mcp_wire_contour --exact`: `passed`
- `cargo xtask gate test the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table --crate camcraft-app --binary mcp_doc_drift --exact`: `passed`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --test agie_native`: `11 passed (the 11 `.refusal` goldens)`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --test conformance`: `7 passed`
- `cargo xtask gate test the_mills_posts_decline_a_plasma_stream_and_the_1300pl --crate camcraft-app --binary plasma_post_refusals --exact`: `passed`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native`: `11 passed`
- `cargo xtask gate test header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound --crate camcraft-post --binary comment_escape --exact`: `passed`
- UI (CWD `crates/ui`): `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-ui --lib -- native_post_dialog`: `3 passed` (3 tests: `native_post_dialog_writes_three_files_and_reports_the_required_work_checks`, `native_post_dialog_refuses_an_invalid_job_name_without_writing_files`, `native_post_dialog_refuses_per_operation_output_without_writing_files`)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: `702 of 702 steps green, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 75.3 minutes wall; 6402 tests passed, 0 failed, 45 ignored`
- `cargo test -j 4 -p camcraft-app --test 'example_catalog*'` (each `example_catalog*` binary by name): `quick steps 253 to 255: `example_catalog` 37 passed and 4 ignored, `example_catalog_adaptive` 1 passed, `example_catalog_edge_work` 1 passed`
- `cargo xtask gate light`: `Result on head 14e01be84: 3 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The steps are light build (release --no-run), motion light: lib and motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel. All 3 steps are ok.`
- No heavy lane (P3).

## Not exercised

- No run on a physical wire EDM control. The posted files do not change, so the control sees the same job.
- A user machine file that states the old post name: the code path is covered by the alias in `validate.rs` and `posting_offer.rs`, but no test loads such a file.
- A setup's own post with the old name from a project file (`mount_dto.rs`): same alias function as the document post, no own test.
- The unit tests inside `crates/post/src/agie/` (if any assert a refusal text) are run only by the quick gate.
- Clippy did not run as a separate step.

## Screenshots

The pictures are headless renders of the UI test harness at the merge base `4c0a157e1` and at head `14e01be84`. Left: before. Right: after.

Post dialog with the native wire EDM post. The post name, the two labels and the option group change.

![Post dialog before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-post-dialog-before.png) ![Post dialog after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-post-dialog-after.png)

Post dialog error for an invalid job name.

![Invalid job name before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-invalid-name-before.png) ![Invalid job name after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-invalid-name-after.png)

Post dialog error for per-operation output.

![Per-operation output before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-per-operation-before.png) ![Per-operation output after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-per-operation-after.png)

Status line after a native job post.

![Status line before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-status-line-before.png) ![Status line after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/1a370768f6ffc76cd53068edf2ae564424da0371/3598/3598-status-line-after.png)

## Decisions

See [docs/decisions/3537-wire-post-name.md](docs/decisions/3537-wire-post-name.md): a save writes the new name; the machine-profile refusal keeps the model; `AGIE_QN2` and the user guide's "Agie Control" stay; the receipt value stays; no project file version change.

Process change: yes

Changelog: The native wire EDM post is now named "Native wire EDM job files", and its refusals no longer name the machine brand. Projects, scripts and MCP calls that use the old name "Agie native wire EDM" still select the post.

Effort: medium

Fixes #3537

title: perf(sim): read law (c) band-reach samples through an exact XY index
body:
## Cause

`band_reach` (`crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs:72-80` on main) slices the model at each distinct end Z of a cutting move (`rest.islands_at`). It adds the boundary samples of each slice to ONE sample set. Then it tests each band disc of each move against the whole set (`reach.rs:180-193`). The cost is moves x planes x samples. A ramp entry ends each move at its own Z, so the cost grows with the square of the moves.

## Fix

- A new private index, `SampleGrid` (`crates/sim/src/verify/sample_grid.rs`), holds the samples. It keeps each sample one time for each exact bit pattern, and puts the samples in square XY cells.
- Each band disc reads only the cells that its box touches. The box is wider than the disc by a relative 1e-9, against rounding.
- A sample or a query that the grid cannot place (NaN, infinity, very far out, a box wider than 64 cells, a bad cell width) is read by all queries, or the query reads all samples.
- The sample set stays ONE set for all planes. The sweep (c3) gets the deduplicated samples.
- `band_reach` now calls `band_reach_counted`, which returns `ReachStats` (slices asked, sample tests). Only the tests read it.

## Why the findings are identical

- The law reads no plane of a sample: a sample from a plane far below a move can convict it. So this PR does NOT split the planes.
- Each reading of a sample (`in_stock`, `surface`, `part_at`) is pure in the sample. The verdict of a disc is a max (part, then stock, then clean). The order and a repeated sample cannot change it.
- The grid gives a superset of the samples that the old distance skip kept. Where a NaN makes the old skip fail, the grid reads the sample too.
- The sweep (c3) uses a max and a memo keyed by the exact bits (`sweep.rs`), so the deduplicated set gives the same answer.
- The old function stays as a test-only reference, `crates/sim/src/verify/reach_reference.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`, line for line, plus two counters). `verify::reach_tests` compares the warnings, in order, and the slice count.

Equivalence cases (`indexed_band_reach_keeps_every_finding_of_the_pooled_scan`, `degenerate_paths_match_the_pooled_scan_and_do_not_panic`, and the count pin):
1. planar rings round a boss, clear (Area and Boundary mode);
2. planar rings 1 mm off the boss walls: real `ShankHit { part: true }` findings;
3. a helix of 216 chords (many planes);
4. many-plane ramps of 400, 500 and 2000 moves, clear of the wall;
5. the same ramps with the shank 1 mm into the wall (real findings);
6. leaning rings whose pose changes at each move (the sweep c3 runs and finds hits);
7. an empty path, and moves with NaN and infinite coordinates.

## Counts (`ReachStats.sample_tests`; old = the reference, the code on main)

| Path | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| ramp 500 moves, shank 2 mm short of the wall | 2,004,000 | 0 |
| ramp 2000 moves, the same | 32,016,000 | 0 |
| ramp 500 moves, shank 1 mm into the wall | 1,394,117 | 20,192 |
| ramp 2000 moves, the same | 22,197,103 | 322,697 |

The slices stay one for each distinct plane (500 and 2000). A disc near a wall still reads the wall samples of every plane: each plane's section has its own vertices on the wall, and an exact law must read them. The decision file has the reasons: `docs/decisions/3588-band-reach-sample-index.md`.

The tangency law (b) slices one time for each distinct Z also. The slice is its cost, so it needs its own design: #3593 (P3).

## Gate (debug, final head)

- Pins (sim lib, `verify::reach_tests` and `verify::sample_grid`): 5 of 5 pass, 0.71 s.
  - `indexed_band_reach_keeps_every_finding_of_the_pooled_scan`
  - `degenerate_paths_match_the_pooled_scan_and_do_not_panic`
  - `a_many_plane_ramp_reads_only_the_samples_near_its_discs`
  - `repeats_are_kept_once_and_every_near_sample_is_found`, `unplaceable_samples_and_queries_fall_back_to_all`
- All `sim suites` steps (`cargo xtask gate batch --only "sim suites"`): 92 of 92 pass, 0 stalled, 3.6 min.
- App binaries, one by one (`cargo test -p camcraft-app --test <name>`), all pass:

title: fix(2d): enter a dead-end later Outside pass by a ramp along the pass
body:
## What changed

With "Pass starts at: Outside", a later pass of 2D Offset or 2D Pocket (Waterline or Offset rings) that starts at a dead end now enters by a ramp along its own pass. Before, it entered by a plunge or a helix into uncut stock (#3567).

**Maintainer decision** (issue #3567, 2026-11-22): "At a dead end of a later pass of 2D Offset with "Pass starts at: Outside", the tool enters with **a ramp along the pass**." The coordinator's standing-word decision (#3567, 23:24Z) accepts the ramp at the ramp angle and names the ramp angle as the control of the load.

**The entry.**
- `level_order::order` marks each later pass of an Outside plan that no lead-in reaches (`LevelPlan::ramp_starts`).
- `ladder_links::pass_link` calls `level_ramp_entry::dead_end_ramp` first. At a marked start, the tool goes down by the existing ramp fallback: the zig-zag along the start of the pass (`descent::ramp_fallback`).
- The ramp angle is the entry's ramp angle, or 3 degrees (`links::DEFAULT_RAMP_ANGLE`) when the operation sets none. The leg limit is the entry's maximum ramp length.
- The ramp starts at the material top of the level plus the plunge height. The last leg lands on the pass start at depth. The pass then cuts the ramped stretch again at the floor.
- The ramp lead is thinned by Douglas-Peucker within `ARC_FIT_TOL` (0.01 mm). Each kept point is a vertex of the pass.

## Review items (review of e7ae538a3)

1. **No silent plunge.** `level_ramp_entry::too_short_at` checks each dead end at the deepest descent of any cut level. A dead end that is too short for the ramp sends the area to the Auto order with `StartSide::ramp_fallback_note`. That note carries `RINGS_FALLBACK`, so the op raises `Warning::StrategyFallback`. If the ladder still cannot plan the ramp, it names that on the path. Pinned by `a_dead_end_too_short_for_the_ramp_falls_back_to_pure_auto`, `a_dead_end_too_short_for_the_ramp_is_found` and `the_ramp_fallback_note_is_a_rings_fallback`.
2. **Slope law in the pin.** `late_entry_cut` counts a descending feed as a ramp only when it is at or under the ramp angle plus 0.05 degrees and on the pass path (within 0.02 mm of a floor feed). A steeper feed counts like a plunge (`a_steep_straight_feed_is_not_a_ramp`). The pin asserts that a ramp ran. New pins:
   - `outside_dead_end_entries_are_no_steeper_than_the_ramp_angle`
   - `outside_floor_under_each_dead_end_ramp_is_cut`
   - `outside_dead_end_ramps_width_reading_of_the_stepover_band` (it reads the band width; it is not a proof against a full-width cut)
3. **A replaced entry is named.** When the ramp replaces the user's Plunge, Helix or Arc entry, the path says so one time, in the #2265 stand-in form (`level_ramp_entry::stand_in_note`, pinned by `a_replaced_entry_is_named`).
4. **The trigger.** Only marked dead ends get the ramp. The first entry of each level and the ring 0 pieces keep the entry of main: a helix or a plunge into solid stock at the first entry is normal and outside this issue. The Auto-order plan after a completeness-guard fallback has no marks, so it stays pure Auto (pinned byte for byte by `a_dead_end_too_short_for_the_ramp_falls_back_to_pure_auto`). The ladder does not scan the earlier moves with `plunge_law::into_solid` at each pass link.
5. **The ramp, in plain words.** The ramp is an entry into uncut stock at a dead end. Where the ring cut before does not reach the dead end, the ramp cuts a slot at nearly the full tool width, at the ramp angle. After the ramp, the pass cuts at one stepover. The ramp angle is the control. Measured on the band of the pins (tool D8, stepover 4):
   - About 25 percent of the tool disc (about 12.6 mm2 of 50.3 mm2) is uncut stock at the start of each of the 8 ramps.
   - The band width during the ramps is 4.78 mm at most, under the limit of 5.375 mm.
   - The earlier "83 percent" number was the stock that each helix of main cut over its whole orbit (332.88 mm2 / 8 = 41.6 mm2), not the stock in the disc at the start.
   - Each ramp runs at 3.000 degrees from Z 2.0 to Z -3.0 over 95.41 mm along the pass.
   - The decision file `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md` says this and quotes the two decisions.
6. **`levels.rs` does not grow.** It has 456 lines (459 on main). The builders are in the new module `level_ramp_entry.rs`.
7. **The file collision with #3566.** This PR keeps `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs` and moves its grid to `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement/grid.rs`. #3566 must drop its copy, or take its four sibling pins onto this file after this PR merges.

## Readings

- The late-entry pin `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock`: 332.88 mm2 on main, 0.00 mm2 with the ramp.
- `pass_start_levels`: 7 of 7, with no limit changed.

## The slow pin is a test-speed problem, not a block

The verification of `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` is slow. It is a test-speed problem, filed as #3587 (`P5`). The verifier speed is filed as #3588 (fix PR #3595, draft). Neither issue blocks #3577.

Readings on this head (`d41c2b76a`):
- `pocket_pass_start`: 5 passed of 6. The sixth test, `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`, did not complete. It stopped at 29 min 23 s. The earlier run tripped the 15-min stall watchdog at 961 s.
- Every other suite is green:
  - motion `pass_start_engagement` 6/6, `pass_start_levels` 7/7;
  - motion lib `machining2d` 267 passed and 10 ignored, `level_ramp_entry` 4/4;
  - app `offset_pass_start` 4/4, `golden_cl` 33/33, `conformance` 7/7, `adaptive_pass_start` 4/4, `bore_pass_start` 3/3;
  - the catalogs 37/1/1;
  - clippy clean;
  - the light lane 2 twins green.

Where the time goes (temporary timers, removed):
- The motion plan and emit take 0.21 s (8850 moves).
- In the verifier (`camcraft_sim::verify::verify_bodies`), tangency takes 34.7 s for 2232 ramp moves. `reach::band_reach` does not finish in more than 3 minutes.
- Each ramp move ends at its own Z. The verifier cuts a new slice of the model at each distinct Z (`Rest::islands_at`). `band_reach` adds the boundary samples of each slice to one sample set and tests each move against all of them.

## Gate

The readings above are the gate of this head. The pinning tests are in `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs`. The motion lib pins are in `level_ramp_entry`, `pass_start`, `level_rings` and `level_order`.

## Not exercised

- No machine run. No posted G-code was read on a controller.
- No release-build run time of the fig8 Outside pocket.
- Adaptive with Outside keeps its old entry at dead ends.
- No heavy lane (P2, AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

Changelog: 2D Offset and 2D Pocket Outside: a later pass that starts at a dead end now enters by a ramp along the pass at the entry's ramp angle (3 degrees by default), not by a plunge or helix into uncut stock. At a dead end, the worst sampled start cuts with about 25 percent of the tool disc in uncut stock (12.6 mm2 of 50.3 mm2 for the 4.780 mm band), so the zig-zag cuts a slot at nearly full tool width at 3 degrees. A dead end too short for the ramp cuts the area in the Auto order, and the path names it.

title: test(2d): port the offset engagement pins
body:
Ports three engagement pins from PR #3439 onto main's Pass start law
(`crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs` and `level_order.rs`).
The change is test-only. It changes no product code.

## What is ported

- `outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots`: Outside on a synthetic
  figure-eight band cuts no wider than 1.5 stepovers over any 3 tool
  radii of floor feed. Main pins this law only in the ignored heavy app
  test `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`. This pin gives
  default-suite coverage.
- `inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band`: Inside on the round-part
  band leaves less than 0.5 mm2 of stock off the part wall. It checks
  both climb directions.
- `auto_on_the_band_slots_so_the_measure_sees_a_slot`: Auto (core first)
  on the same band slots. This pin is the positive control for the width
  measure.

| Test | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots | pass | 0.94 s |
| inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band | pass | 2.08 s |

`cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_engagement -- --exact <name>`.

title: feat(3d): add waterlines switch to skip steep-flank ring pass
body:
﻿## What changed

- Added `waterlines: bool` (default `true`) across `Finish3DParams`, `OpParams::Finish3D`, `ParamsDto::Finish3D`, MCP tools (`add_operation`, `edit_operation`, `list_operation_types`), project serialization (`#[serde(default = "default_true")]`), and the 3D Finish Passes UI tab (`Steep flanks`: `Waterlines` / `Leave uncut` with an inline consequence note).
- Updated `rings_and_tail_with_trim` and `swarf_multi` so `waterlines: false` skips the steep-flank waterline ring pass on shallow-first patterns, emits a visible steep-flank note on `Toolpath::notes` (surfaced in the UI status banner and MCP output), keeps uncut steep-flank stock visible to downstream rest checks, and refuses all-steep or no-shallow-cut models with `GenError::Empty`.
- Refused `waterlines: false` by name for ring-dependent patterns (`Waterline`, `Blend`, `Morph`), and hid the switch in the UI for patterns without a steep-flank waterline pass (`Waterline`, `Blend`, `Morph`, `Flat`, `Pencil`, `Corner`, `Geodesic`).
- Split `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/validate.rs` from `params.rs` for the 400-line file rule, added pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_waterlines.rs`, `crates/app/tests/operations.rs`, `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs`, `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`, and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`, and recorded design decisions in `docs/decisions/2811-finish-waterlines-switch.md`.

Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first)

## What changed

- Add `OpType::Pocket` to `do_not_touch_applies` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`.
- Update `do_not_touch_unsupported` to list `2D Pocket, 2D Offset and 3D Pocket`.
- Update the `set_operation_do_not_touch` text in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Wire `OpParams::Pocket` with `avoid_spec` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` to `pocket_avoid_entered_with_relief`, `rest_pocket_avoid_with_relief`, and `rest_pocket_previous_avoid_with_relief`.
- Extract per-level planning (`plan_avoid_level`), relief checks (`check_reliefs_avoid`), crossing-free checks (`enforce_level_crossing_free`), and rest dispatch (`emit_rest_avoid`) into `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid_level.rs`.
- Unify plain and rest avoid paths in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, and `rest_prior.rs` under `pocket_avoid_over`.
- Check overhead keep-out zones up to `p.clearance_z.max(z)` so entry rapids and final clearance lifts clear overhead obstacles.
- Guard `Descent::Helix` (`m.solid_restart`) and `entry_restart` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs` and `descent_dive.rs` with `helix_clears_prior`, `find_clear_helix_raw`, `moves_clear`, and `helix_cross_fallback`.
- Record between-pass `KeepDown` chords in `LinkState.level` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs`.
- Derive `Clone` for `LinkTally`, `LinkState`, and `WalkState`.
- Add pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/avoid_pocket.rs`, `crates/app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`, and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`.
- Record the design choice in `docs/decisions/3345-do-not-touch-2d-pocket.md`.

## Cause

- `do_not_touch_applies` refused `OpType::Pocket`, and `OpParams::Pocket` in `generate.rs` dropped `avoid_spec`.
- `pocket_avoid` supported plain 2D Offset only. It lacked `PreHole` entries and rest plans, and it checked overhead obstacles only up to `retract_z`.
- When keep-out zones trimmed inner passes across depths under `OffsetRings` + `KeepDown` + `Helix`, restarted helices overlapped earlier helices in XY at shared entry depths.

- After the final edit, `camcraft-app --test mcp_doc_drift` passed all 6 tests.
- After the final edit, `camcraft-ui --lib` passed all 4 `egui_app::tests::do_not_touch` tests (`pocket2d_boundaries_shows_pick_protected_and_takes_viewport_click`, `unsupported_op_shows_do_not_touch_note_without_pick_button`, `geometry_boundaries_shows_do_not_touch_controls_rows_and_viewport_marks`, `avoid_marks_cache_reuses_still_frames_and_follows_input_changes`).

title: fix(turning): part-off states the piece kept and a back stock
body:
Stacked on #3472 (merge #3472 first). Before #3472 merges, this PR stays based on `main`; it carries the #3472 commits until then.

## What changed

The Part (part-off) operation gets one setting, `kerf: PartKerf` (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting_law.rs`). It has two values:

- `kept`: the piece that is the finished part.
  - `CutOff` (the default) is the #3452 rule. The whole kerf is on the chuck side.
  - `Chuck` keeps the piece in the chuck. The whole kerf is on the free-end side, and a stub comes off the free end.
- `back_stock` (mm, 0 or more, default 0): the whole kerf stands this far off the parting plane, into the scrap side. The part keeps that much on its end face for a later facing pass.

Where the setting is:

- Kernel: `part_in` reads the scrap side and the kerf flank from the setting.
- Gouge law: `part_kerf_refusal_for` judges the kerf against the part that `kept` names. It treats the back stock as part material. The old `part_kerf_refusal` calls it with the default.
- Flipped setup (`job.rs`): a setup that holds the part end for end refuses only the default now. The refusal names the setting: "Set 'The part is' to 'Chuck piece'". With `Chuck`, the part-off generates.
- Project file: the keys `kept` (`cut_off` / `chuck`) and `back_stock` (`project/part_kerf_dto.rs`). Each key is written only when it is not the default.
- Page: the Passes tab of the Part op has "The part is" (Cut-off piece / Chuck piece) and "Back stock". Apply rides `EditOperationParams`.
- MCP: `edit_operation` patches `kept` and `back_stock` through `EditOperationParams`. No new tool is necessary.
- Validation: a negative or non-finite back stock is refused at the command door (`is_sane`), in the kernel and in the verdict.
- Stamp: the setting is folded only when it is not the default. Thus no op saved before the setting reads stale.

The decision record: `docs/decisions/3469-part-kept-side.md`.

## Cause

#3472 put the whole kerf on the chuck side, and no parameter could change the side. In a flipped second setup the chuck holds the finished part. #3472 had to refuse every part-off there, which refuses a legal program (issue comments of 2026-11-22).

## Readings (3 mm GT-0300 blade, orientation 2: the -Z corner is posted)

| case | kerf | posted Z |
|---|---|---|
| #3452 pin, end face Z-70, default | Z-73..-70 | Z-73 (no change) |
| same, back stock 0.5 | Z-73.5..-70.5 | Z-73.5 |
| same, chuck piece | refused: "nothing to part ... stands wholly on the free-end side (higher Z) ... set 'The part is' to 'Cut-off piece'" | - |
| stubbed pin in the OP20 flip setup, plane Z-14, default | refused by name (names 'Chuck piece') | - |
| same, chuck piece | Z-14..-11 | Z-14 (the part's end face) |
| motion: part Z0..70 in the chuck, stub to Z84, plane Z70, chuck piece | Z70..73 | - |
| same, chuck piece, back stock 1 | Z71..74 | - |

## Tests

New pins. Each was red on the unchanged code (#3472 head 6c18258d1): the motion and app pins did not compile (no `PartKerf`, no `kerf` field), and the flip pin is refused there.

- `crates/motion/tests/turning_part_kept.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `the_default_setting_parts_the_3452_case_as_before`
  - `a_back_stock_moves_the_whole_kerf_into_the_bar`: the kerf, and the refusal of the default kerf "0.500 mm into the 0.500 mm back stock".
  - `the_chuck_piece_turns_the_kerf_to_the_free_end`: the kerf, no rule note, and the refusal of the default kerf on that model ("3.000 mm past", "free-end side (higher Z)").
  - `the_chuck_piece_with_no_model_below_the_plane_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_back_stock_that_is_not_a_size_is_refused`: -0.1, NaN, infinity, in the kernel and in the verdict.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_part_off_kerf.rs` (4 new tests):
  - `a_flipped_setup_keeping_the_chuck_piece_cuts_the_stub_off_the_free_end`: generates, posts Z-14.
  - `a_back_stock_posts_the_kerf_that_far_into_the_bar`: posts Z-73.5.
  - `the_chuck_piece_with_nothing_in_the_chuck_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_kerf_setting_is_an_undoable_edit_and_rides_the_project_file`: no key at the default, a negative back stock refused by `EditOperationParams::new`, edit, undo, redo, save and open.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_part_kerf.rs` (new): `edit_operation_sets_the_kept_piece_and_back_stock_and_undo_restores_them`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/part_kerf_tests.rs` (new): `the_kept_piece_row_names_both_pieces_and_its_pick_applies_and_undoes`.

Changed pin (expected): `a_flipped_setup_refuses_the_part_off_by_name` now asks for the new refusal text ("cannot keep the cut-off piece", "'Chuck piece'").

Mechanical: each `OpParams::Part` and `PartParams` literal in the tests gets `kerf: Default::default()`.

### Mutation checks (each guard put back to the old code, then restored)

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| kernel uses `chuck_side()` and the plane (ignores the setting) | RED: 3 tests of `turning_part_kept` |
| verdict ignores the back stock zone | RED: `a_back_stock_moves_the_whole_kerf_into_the_bar` |
| verdict uses `chuck_side()` (ignores `kept`) | RED: 2 chuck-piece tests |
| flip refusal unconditional again (the #3472 code) | RED: `a_flipped_setup_keeping_the_chuck_piece_cuts_the_stub_off_the_free_end` |
| no back stock check at the command door | RED: `the_kerf_setting_is_an_undoable_edit_and_rides_the_project_file` |

After the restore, all pins are green.

### Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans 730 steps (the motion change reaches every app binary). Thus each touched binary ran alone, debug, on head c6230e2a0:

- motion: `--lib` 536 passed (10 ignored); `turning_part_kept` 5; `turning_part_kerf` 6; `turning_blade` 11; `turning_stock` 5; `turning_contour_stock` 4.
- app: `lathe_part_off_kerf` 8; `mcp_part_kerf` 1; `lathe_blade_corner` 4; `catalog_groove_part_off` 1; `lathe_post` 7; `lathe_post_inch` 6; `turning_blade` 14; `setup_align_lathe` 4; `turning_stock_approach` 3; `drill_prior` 12; `coarse_laws` 6; `project_roundtrip` 76; `mcp_enum_patch` 3; `--lib part` 17.
- app `example_catalog -- groove cone`: 5 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread` (`example_catalog.rs:311`, "the part-off reaches the axis"). It is in #3472, not in this PR. #3472 changed `cone-thread.nc` to `G01 X0. Z12.`, but the test still asks for `Z13.5`. This PR does not touch either file, and the two `regenerates` tests pass (the default posts the same bytes).
- ui: `--lib` 1432 passed (7 ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Heavy lanes

GREEN on `c6230e2a0c5c6f9a7631c5a3386cc06e326310e1`: **244 steps, 0 failed**, 51.7 minutes. The gate ran all motion and app heavy targets, including the release build. The tool accepted the known-fail entries for #1950 and #2849 as expected.

Command: `RUSTC_WRAPPER= CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`.

The gate started against current upstream `9a7de37812ad1c891b61579332f25be7ab55906e`. The shared upstream ref later advanced to `f35202134ec002b775fc33fbc2220434331c4449`. Explicit-base dry runs select the same 244 steps and all 244 Cargo commands for both bases.

### Full catalog comparison

Command: `RUSTC_WRAPPER= CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 cargo test --release -j16 -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog -- --test-threads=16`.

- Published PR head: **RED**, 36 passed, 1 failed, 4 ignored. `turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread` fails at `example_catalog.rs:311`: `the part-off reaches the axis`.
- Clean upstream `9a7de37812ad1c891b61579332f25be7ab55906e` (also with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`): **GREEN**, 37 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored. The same cone-thread test passes.
- All four ignored catalog tests passed in the heavy gate. They do not replace the full catalog suite.

This round changes no code, goldens, or PR head. It verifies only the owed heavy lanes and catalog suite. It does not resolve the latest review's code or conflict findings. No new pin or mutation check applies to this verification-only round. Quick, clippy, and UI checks were not repeated. The PR remains a draft with `needs-rework` and `conflicts`. No `merge-ready` label was added.

## Goldens moved

None. The default setting posts the same program. No `.nc`, `.cl` or catalog file changed.

## Not exercised

- A real control or machine. Lathe posts other than `fanuc-lathe.cps`.
- The UI in a live window (the page is tested through the kittest harness).

## Overlaps

- #3472: the stack base. It changes `parting_law.rs`, `parting.rs` and the flip refusal in `job.rs`, which this PR changes again.
- These open PRs touch the same files, but other functions or other kinds. None changes the Part variant, the Part page arm or the part-off law. Whichever merges second refreshes:
  - `operation/types/params.rs`, `project/params.rs`, `project/params_impl.rs`, `operation/kinds.rs`: #3494, #3441, #3439, #3426, #3402, #3391, #3387, #3353, #3283, #3251, #3103, #3058, #2890, #2831.
  - `operation/types/sane.rs`: #3426, #3402, #3283, #3251, #3058, #2831.
  - `operation/job.rs`: #3458, #3283, #3251, #3115, #3059, #3058, and older ones.
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mod.rs` (one `mod` line): many open UI PRs.

Effort: high (not escalated).

Changelog: Part (part-off) has a new setting. "The part is" chooses the cut-off piece (the default, as before) or the chuck piece, which cuts a stub off the free end of a part held end for end. "Back stock" moves the whole kerf that far off the parting plane, so the part keeps material on its end face for a later facing pass. The gouge check judges the kerf against the part that the setting keeps. A part-off in a setup that holds the part end for end is refused only when the setting keeps the cut-off piece, and the refusal names the setting. Existing projects post the same program.

Fixes #3469

title: fix(post): post a short arc whose written ends share one angle as a straight move
body:
Stacked on #3471 (merge #3471 first).

## What changed
- `arcFateOf` (`crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs`) has one more rule. The written start and the written end differ, but they are on one ray from the written centre (the same angle). Or one end is on the written centre. If the record turns half a circle or less, the answer is `"linear"`. The post writes its straight feed move.
- The rule reads the numbers of the written words. It uses only the zero of the cross product and the sign of the dot product. A mirrored axis or a lathe diameter word does not change these.
- A record whose own ends in the stream are on one ray (stream sweep 0) stays an arc. `emitArcWithRadius` reads that as a full turn.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps` now write the feed move for `"linear"` in their meridian arc path. Before, they wrote no block for any answer that was not `"arc"`.
- The old inline sweep code moved into the helper `_arcSweep`. Its behaviour did not change.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3474-same-angle-arc.md`.

## Cause
The #3442 guard compares only the written ends. When the ends differ only along the radius, the guard returned `"arc"`. On the parent branch every mill post wrote such a block. Examples:
- Fanuc mm: `G01 X10.011 Y5.` then `G03 X10.01 Y5. Z5.5 I-0.011 J0. F180`.
- LinuxCNC inch: `G1 X0.4011 Y0.2` then `G3 X0.401 Y0.2 Z0.2165 I-0.0011 J0 F7.09`.

The start and the end are at the same angle about the centre. The radii are 0.011 and 0.010. RS-274 / ISO 6983 reads an arc whose end is at its start angle as a full turn. No control ran these blocks. A straight move is correct for each reading.

## Tests
New file `crates/post/tests/same_angle_arcs.rs`:
- `fanuc_and_linuxcnc_post_a_same_angle_arc_as_a_straight_move`: Fanuc and LinuxCNC, mm and inch. No arc block, and a straight move to the written end.
- `every_post_writes_a_same_angle_arc_as_its_straight_move`: all 14 mill posts in each unit that they offer, and the two lathes. The output is byte-equal to the straight feed to the same end. TinyG writes 4 decimals in mm. There the mm witness is a visible arc, and the test asserts that it stays one arc.
- `arc_fate_reads_a_same_angle_short_arc_as_a_straight_move`: the rule. Same angle, end on centre, a long CW record, an opposite end, a normal arc, and a stream sweep of zero.

All three were red on the parent head (#3471, `40e1baae7`).

Mutations (each put back, then restored):
- The guard of the parent PR: all 3 pins red.
- The `fanuc-lathe.cps` call site of the parent PR: `every_post_...` red (`fanuc-lathe mm`).
- The `tormach-lathe.cps` call site of the parent PR: `every_post_...` red (`tormach-lathe mm`).
- No `sweep > 1e-9` term: `radius_arcs::near_180_and_full_circle_arcs_in_all_planes_hold_chord_and_center` and `arc_fate_...` red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-3471` (the parent head): 75 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
None.

## Not exercised
- No control ran the blocks. The reading of the controls is from RS-274 / ISO 6983, not from a run.
- A written end behind the written start (a written sweep of nearly a full turn on a short record). We found no input that makes it. It is recorded as dropped in the decision.
- The rule uses the written absolute centre word. The control's centre is the start plus the written `I J`. The two can differ by one output step.
- Mill-turn, plasma and wire posts get the rule through the same `arcFate` call. They have no witness in the new file.

## Overlaps
- Stacked on #3471: it adds `arc_guard.rs` and `arcFateOf`, which this PR changes. Retarget this PR to `main` before #3471 merges.

Changelog: A post now writes a straight move for a very small arc whose written start and end have the same angle about the centre. Before, a control could read the block as a full turn.

Fixes #3474

title: fix(multiaxis): rotate the rotaries before the first five-axis approach descent
body:
## What changed

Five-axis generators set the first station's pose on the modal builder
and then pushed the descend to first contact, so the rotary swing rode
the approach move: the machine turned the A/C head while the tool
descended, and the ball swept through unknown air and through the rim
it approached.

The fix splits the approach. The pose is stated as its own zero-travel
Rapid (a standstill rotary index - the tip held on the hop plane, or at
the tip the machine already holds), and the Plunge/cut descends under
the pose already stated:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve.rs` (`contour_curve`): every
  chain's approach swings first, then plunges.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs` (the stamp emit loop, all
  posed kinds - parallel5d, flow5d, swarf5d, rough, contour5d): at
  every rapid-to-cut re-entry where the pose changes, the swing is
  emitted at a standstill before the cut. Intermediate cut moves keep
  the modal tilt law unchanged.

No new `MoveKind`. The builder already keeps a zero-travel move whose
pose changed (it drops one only when the tip AND the pose both stand),
and the post already solves a zero-travel segment as a pure rotary
reorientation (`ds_tip == 0` in `crates/post/src/post/g93.rs`), so the
swing always commands. That is the answer to the zero-travel question:
the swing is a zero-travel rapid, not a short travel move - a travel
move would drag the tip sideways while the head turns, and a dropped
zero-travel move cannot occur, because a drop needs the pose to match
the held one, in which case no rotation is due.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 28 steps, 0 failed
  (motion lib 536 passed, multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough,
  pivot5d, swarf_pose_continuity, app operations, posed_contact and the
  rest all green).
- The existing laws were amended where the swing touches them, each in
  its own terms: a TRAVEL rapid still inherits its pose
  (`rapids_hold_the_pose_they_inherit`, `rapid_pose_contract` - the
  zero-travel index is the second legal way a rapid states a pose,
  beside the swarf link's ball-centred swing); the air-link ratchet
  counts travel links only; the pivot-law ball readers skip the
  swing (it cuts nothing) through `no_swings`/`sans_swings` helpers.
- A decision record sits in `docs/decisions/3414-approach-rotary-order.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `the_approach_rotates_before_it_descends` (crates/motion/tests/pivot5d.rs):
  a zero-travel rotary swing precedes the first descend; the plunge
  holds the pose the swing stated; no pose change rides any move that
  crosses from air to material, over contour_curve, parallel5d, flow5d
  and swarf5d.

## What was not exercised

- No posted G-code golden was regenerated (the post's pure-rotary path
  is covered by its own suite; the swing was not posted end to end on
  a real machine file).
- The heavy lanes were not run; the diff touches `camcraft-motion`, so
  the release-tier lane check stays with the review/cut.

## Changelog

Five-axis approach moves rotate the machine to the first pose before
the tool descends to the part, no longer while it descends.

Fork synced at v0.25.0.

Fixes #3414

title: fix(multiaxis): close the Rotary Offset Zigzag levels with a ring that skips the seam
body:
## What changed

Rotary Offset Zigzag levels now finish their walls with a ring, as the
planar #3129 levels already do. On the wrap the plan drops only the
seam's own edges: a boundary loop that spans a whole period wraps the
seam, and its two cover-end edges are the seam's two copies at one
azimuth. That loop's ring keeps one period of boundary per leftover arc;
each arc arrives open and ends on the seam copy of its start azimuth -
closed on the work - while the rows cut the seam columns. A loop that
wraps no azimuth closes exactly as the planar ring always did. The
no-seam path is byte-for-byte the old `zigzag_ringed_passes` behaviour.

Before the fix the wrap kept its rows alone, so every wall perpendicular
to the rows kept cusps between row ends. Measured on the new test's
D-flat: the worst wall scallop falls from 0.071 mm to under 0.02 mm at
every level between the flat and the skin.

Placement: `machining2d::pocket_zigzag::ringed_passes` (the seam law,
one `Option<f64>` period), called from `machining3d::hsm::plan_level`.
Decision record: `docs/decisions/3168-rotary-zigzag-seam-rings.md`.

## Pinning tests

New suite `crates/motion/tests/rotary_zigzag_rings.rs`:

- `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` - on a developed cover two
  periods wide, the target band's ring cuts every azimuth once: no
  azimuth bin takes radial feed runs in both directions, and the band's
  walls stay within the wall-reach bound. This is the failure the old
  "a ring there would cut one seam line twice" comment feared.
- `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` - a D-flat bar wraps and its edge
  walls (perpendicular to the rows) finish within the wall-reach bound
  at every level between the flat and the skin. Run against the unfixed
  tree it fails with `scallop 0.071 mm`.

## What was not exercised

- The Adaptive seam law (`Seam::crossed_by`, the named refusals) is
  untouched and its own suites still cover it.
- No posted G-code golden was re-recorded; the change alters Zigzag
  wrap toolpaths by adding rings, which the level law's own tests do not
  pin.
- The heavy lanes reached by a `motion` diff were not run locally; the
  review runs them per AGENTS.md.

Changelog: Rotary Offset Zigzag levels finish their walls with a closing
ring that skips the seam, removing wall cusps on flats and other
perpendicular walls.

Fixes #3168

title: fix(3d): keep Finish3D clear of protected items
body:
Stacked on #3462 (merge #3462 first)

## What changed

3D Finish now accepts protected faces and edge chains.
The generator clips cuts outside a keep-out for the flutes, shank and holder.
The keep-out covers tip heights from the cut bottom to the clearance plane.
It rotates with the work coordinates.
Rapid links rise above protected items.
The final full-tool check refuses remaining contact and names the item.
The path notes that material beside protected items can remain unfinished.
Without protected items, the moves stay the same.
The existing command supplies undo and redo.
MCP help and its committed reference now name the supported kinds.

The change reuses `AvoidSpec::keepout_region`, `finish_clip::clip_path` and the existing WCS transform.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/3347-finish3d-do-not-touch.md`.

Review round 1 (head `f7ff1d080`):

- The branch now contains `upstream/main` `054c1e24b` (a merge commit, no conflict).
- The Trace fixture of `do_not_touch_click.rs` uses the 1,400 px height of Finish3D. The "Not taken" Start point and Exit point groups of #3324 moved "Pick protected" below the 1,100 px harness.

## Cause

Finish3D was absent from `do_not_touch_applies`.
Its generator did not read the protected geometry.

## Tests

App pins in `do_not_touch_finish3d`:

- `finish3d_accepts_protected_faces_and_edges_and_keeps_unprotected_moves`
- `finish3d_keeps_flutes_shank_and_holder_clear_of_a_protected_face`
- `finish3d_refuses_an_impossible_protected_cut_by_name_and_blocks_post`
- `finish3d_lifts_links_above_a_protected_face_higher_than_clearance`
- `finish3d_rotated_wcs_keeps_the_protected_face_in_setup_coordinates`

UI pins:

- `finish3d_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click`
- `trace_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click`

The first app pin failed on unchanged production code with the unsupported-kind diagnostic.
All five app pins and the UI pins pass.
The checks include independent tool-band samples and the live protected-geometry check.
They cover a named refusal, blocked NC output, undo and redo, and unchanged unprotected moves.

Each mutation failed semantically, then passed after restoration:

- Restore the old upstream allow-list: protected Finish3D picks are refused.
- Restore the old upstream generator: the holder violates the protected face clearance.
- Skip the keep-out clipping: the final check refuses the holder contact.
- Skip the WCS conversion: the rotated path meets the protected face.
- Skip rapid routing: a link meets the tall protected face with the shank.
- Remove the named clip error: the refusal omits the protected item.
- Trace fixture at 1,100 px (the old height) on the merged tree: `trace_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click` fails at line 82 ("the group is armed"). At 1,400 px, all 8 `do_not_touch` UI tests pass.

## Heavy lanes

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on head `f7ff1d080`:

- Plan: `app heavy: every target` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` changed).
- Result: 208 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (64.6 min). This includes `app heavy: example_catalog`.

## Screenshots

The Boundary group on the Geometry tab, before (`upstream/main` `6e641dac7`) and after (`f7ff1d080`).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Trace | ![before trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/14b2955c7b4c1c7a74aab0681f549db790454316/3495/before-trace-boundary.png) | ![after trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/14b2955c7b4c1c7a74aab0681f549db790454316/3495/after-trace-boundary.png) |

title: feat(tools): one tool meridian for each mill kind, split into convex atoms
body:
## What changed

- A new module `camcraft_tools::meridian` adds the tool meridian. The meridian is the cutting outline `rho(z)` of a mill, tip up. It is made of lines and circular arcs.
- `Meridian` uses the `SpunPoint` form (`z`, `r`, signed `arc`). It holds one cutting flag for each segment. A pilot bearing band is a non-cutting segment.
- `Tool::meridian()` gives the meridian of these kinds: `EndMill`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`, `Drill`, `Taper`, `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, `Dovetail`, `Lollipop`.
- `Meridian::atoms(bound, sag)` splits the meridian into convex solids of revolution:
  - a line gives a frustum;
  - an arc that bulges away from the axis gives a torus zone;
  - an arc that bulges toward the axis gives chord frusta (`Bound::Outer`) or tangent frusta (`Bound::Inner`). Each part stays within the sag limit.
- Each atom carries the cutting flag of its segment.
- Degenerate input gives a named `MeridianError`. It never panics.
- No consumer reads the meridian yet. No toolpath, simulation, check or posted output changes.

## Latest review fixes

- Validate the shape dimensions before a calculation or a fallback. Preserve the named errors `NonFinite`, `Negative` and `Short`.
- Normalize the line interpolation before multiplication. The accepted `1e308`-height line returns the correct midpoint radius, `5.5`.
- Reject non-finite segment lengths and unsupported circle coordinates with `OutOfRange`. The documented arc bound is `MAX_ARC_COORD = 1e150`. This bound keeps squared circle terms finite.
- Calculate each circle midpoint from its start and half its delta. This avoids overflow in endpoint sums.

## Cause

This is sub-issue 1 of #3351 (option C, the hybrid shape model). The maintainer asked for tapered and router tooling. Later sub-issues make the consumers read the tool shape through this meridian.

## Tests

Pins:

- `verify::probe_meridian_tests::meridian_atoms_match_cutter_atoms_for_each_mill_kind` (camcraft-sim lib). For 12 tools of each listed kind, the meridian atoms are the solids that `Cutter::atoms` builds today. The test compares `z0`, `z1` and `rho` at 65 heights, within 1e-9 mm. The cases include a ball and a bull nose shorter than the corner, and a cone taller than the flute.
- `meridian::tests::meridian_agrees_with_profile_on_the_cutting_band` (camcraft-tools lib). The meridian agrees with `Tool::profile` at each profile vertex on the cutting band.
- `meridian::tests::concave_arc_outer_bound_contains_and_inner_bound_stays_inside`. For sag limits 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 mm: the outer union contains the arc, the inner union stays inside it, and each sag is under the limit. The bearing band is the one non-cutting atom.
- `meridian::tests::degenerate_meridians_are_refused_by_name`: too few points, zero-length segment, negative radius, non-finite value, arc tighter than its chord, segment that runs back, arc that folds, concave arc through the axis, flag count, bad sag limit, sag limit too fine.
- `meridian::tests::tool_meridian_refuses_bad_tools_by_name`: a kind that is not a mill, NaN, negative and zero diameter, a bull corner over half the diameter, a dovetail that `undercut::refusal` names.

Red before the change: the sim pin did not compile (`E0432: unresolved import camcraft_tools::meridian`, `E0599: no method named meridian`).

The first green run found float dust: `bull: rho(0) 3.0000000298023224 vs 3`. A centre error of 1e-16 gives 3e-8 mm of error at the z extreme of the circle. The fix snaps the centre when an arc end sits at the centre's radius.

Mutation checks (each red, then restored and green):

- fold guard removed: `degenerate_meridians_are_refused_by_name` red (`Ok(..)` vs `Err(ArcFolds(1))`).
- through-axis guard removed: the same test red (`Ok(..)` vs `Err(Negative(1))`).
- outer and inner bounds swapped: `concave_arc_outer_bound_contains_and_inner_bound_stays_inside` red (`outer under the arc at z 4.01`).
- centre snap absent: the sim pin red (`bull: rho(0) 3.0000000298023224 vs 3`).

Final validation for this fix round:

- Head: `0948d7989ab0b8e217dd99193da23acf4a880586`. The gates started with base `74ea8988d800f00d41547ec9d292077d2bc3ddc5`.
- `upstream/main` advanced during the heavy run to `60376ccbbfa52305db6fa880278222e7854fcdbf`. Both bases have the same merge base and the same three-dot diff. The current quick and heavy plans select the same ordered 122 and 243 steps. The completed tests cover the full current selection.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 122 steps passed. The first run passed 80 steps and had 42 build failures from stale seeded kernel and geometry metadata. After a targeted cache clean, all 42 failed steps passed with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`. No source change was needed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 243 steps passed, 0 failed, in 44.8 minutes. The gate checked the declared known failures at their expected assertions.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed in 2 minutes 29 seconds.
- `app suites: example_catalog` ran in the quick gate: 37 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored. All four ignored catalog tests passed in the heavy gate.
- `app suites: solid_law_goldens` ran in the quick gate: 7 passed, 0 failed.
- `meridian::tests::tool_meridian_checks_inputs_before_shape_fallbacks` pins named errors for malformed tool dimensions.
- `meridian::tests::accepted_extreme_meridians_have_finite_correct_radii` pins finite, correct interpolation for accepted extreme inputs.
- `meridian::tests::meridian_refuses_overflowing_lengths_and_circle_ranges` pins named refusals for unsupported segment lengths and circle coordinates.
- Mutation proof: removing the input guard made `tool_meridian_checks_inputs_before_shape_fallbacks` fail on the NaN drill. Restoring the guard made it pass.
- Mutation proof: restoring the old interpolation made `accepted_extreme_meridians_have_finite_correct_radii` fail on a non-finite radius. Restoring the fix made it pass.
- Mutation proof: removing the length guard and circle bounds separately made `meridian_refuses_overflowing_lengths_and_circle_ranges` fail. Each mutation returned `Ok` instead of `OutOfRange`. Each restored check passed.
- All four mutations failed with exit 101. Each restored pin passed with exit 0. All seven meridian tests passed.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog and solid-law golden suites passed. The diff changes no catalog entry or recorded program.

## Not exercised

- No consumer reads the meridian, so no end-to-end path runs through it.
- No real router bit record (roundover, cove) exists yet. The concave-arc tests use a hand-built roundover meridian.

No UI file changes. UI screenshots do not apply.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/3367-tool-meridian.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Tools: a tool meridian (lines and arcs) for each mill kind, split into convex atoms with outer and inner bounds for concave arcs (internal; no output change).

Fixes #3367

title: fix(2d): keep exterior contours at their requested depths
body:
## What changed

Exterior contour rings that the user picks keep every requested depth when the complete cutter-center ring clears the model's XY convex hull.
The sign plate reaches Z 0 and keeps its four tabs.
Picked contours refuse generation when a required deeper section cannot be read.
The error names the section failure and the skipped levels.

The hull proof applies only to picked rings (`contour_on_picked`, through `ladder_picked`).
The whole-model contour and the unpicked region contour keep the plain `ladder`.
A whole-model contour on a broken mesh must refuse when a section cannot be read.
The hull proof skips each section, so it must not hide that refusal.

## Cause

The depth ladder read interior sections even for a cutter outside the complete model footprint.
A failed section could become a false floor.
The picked-ring check accepted this partial path after an earlier level succeeded.

## Tests

Final head: 813e6a8cc. Base: `upstream/main` at 6e641dac7.

Pins:

- `outside_sign_plate_reaches_bottom_with_four_tabs` (motion `contour_outside_floor`) checks every requested depth and four bottom cut runs.
- `picked_ring_refuses_unread_deeper_plane_after_clear_levels` (motion `contour_outside_floor`) checks refusal after earlier levels succeed.
- `whole_model_contour_that_cannot_reach_bottom_is_refused_with_the_stopped_level` (app `contour_whole_step`, unchanged) checks that a whole-model contour on a broken mesh refuses.

Pin proof:

- The first two pins fail when the original `upstream/main` depth code is restored. The plate pin reports floor Z 7.061. The unread-section pin returns a partial path.
- The third pin fails when the hull proof is put back into the shared `ladder`. It reports `deepest=-0.5`, the same failure that the review found. It passes when the fix is restored.

Commands on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 146 steps, 0 failed.
- All 13 app suites whose name starts with `contour`: all pass. `contour_whole_step`: 3 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test contour_outside_floor`: 2 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Gate map gap: the quick gate does not select app `contour_whole_step` for this diff. The suite imports only `camcraft_app` re-exports, so the map does not link it to `motion::machining2d`.

The mesh fixture contains only the `sign` entity's saved triangles from the [reported q04 project](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj).
The test does not import STEP or load the saved toolpath.

## Heavy lanes

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` ran on head 813e6a8cc19ab8598b648ec9f5c4cacc8db5d61e.
The base was `upstream/main` at 6e641dac753020bfed49fec310237eed28448141.
The diff reaches the `motion heavy` and `app heavy` lanes.
Result: green. 244 steps ran, 0 failed. Wall time was 40.3 min.
Known-fail markers from main were red as expected (#1950, #2849).

## Goldens moved

None. `example_catalog` ran green on the final head.
No `.nc` or `.cl` files change.

## Not exercised

The reported project was not run through the GUI or MCP.
The complete post flow for this project was not run.
The regression calls the motion generator on the saved model mesh.
The 0.02 mm allowance, `tab_count: 0`, and bottom-chain variants were not run separately.
`contour_depth.rs` is 436 lines. It was 421 lines before this round, over the 400-line rule. This round adds the `ladder_in` seam. The picked wrapper is in `contour_exterior.rs`.

## Overlaps

None.

title: fix(setup): setups keep their creation order, not their name order
body:
## What changed

- `SetupDef` has a new field `order: Option<u32>`.
- `CreateSetup` writes the next order: one past the highest stored order, 0 for the first setup.
- `CreateSetup` refuses creation when the highest stored order is `u32::MAX`. The refusal preserves the document and program order.
- `setup::setups` sorts by `order`. Setups without an order (older files) sort first, by name. This is the old behaviour for these files.
- The project file saves `order` on the setup row. `PROJECT_VERSION` steps from 76 to 77 (second review). A v76 file has no `order`; it opens unchanged and keeps name order. A v76 reader refuses a v77 file.
- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` states version 77. `deburr_chord_width.rs` now pins `>= 76` and the current version, not the literal 76.
- `add_setup`, `get_job`, `operation_order` and the post all read `setup::setups`. They now all follow the creation order.
- Comments in `setup.rs` that said "by name" now say "program order".

## Cause

`setup::setups` returned the setups in name order. `Front_A90` sorted before `Setup1`. Thus it was listed and posted first, although it took its datum and stock from `Setup1`.

## Tests

- New pin `crates/app/tests/setup_creation_order.rs`:
  - `a_setup_created_second_stays_second_whatever_its_name`: `Setup1`, then `Front_A90` (datum from `Setup1`). The names and the operation order keep the creation order. A third setup goes last. Delete and undo give it back its place.
  - `the_creation_order_survives_save_and_load_and_reaches_the_post`: save, `open_project` over MCP, `get_job` and `add_setup` list the creation order, and the posted program has `Setup1`'s operation before `Front_A90`'s.
- Red before the fix: both tests failed (`left: ["Front_A90", "Setup1"]`).
- Mutations:

title: feat(motion): engrave and trace open and closed sketch chains
body:
Engrave and Trace now follow open and closed chains from a placed sketch. The user can select a profile, individual chains or a layer. The operation preserves the cut direction of lines, arcs and circles. It applies the sketch placement and the work-coordinate rotation to both endpoints and arc centers. A lift separates disconnected strokes and gaps accepted by the drawing tolerance.

Each depth level approaches from the stock surface. The existing stock, fixture, shank and mark-depth checks can hold the post, including jobs that have no part solid. Very short arcs below the post resolution give a diagnostic. A major arc is split into two arcs that keep its center and sweep. #3442 tracks the separate case where a native Fanuc post accepts a short arc supplied directly in an intermediate file.

The 18-move CL fixture contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes.
