title: feat(text): place typed text in a TrueType outline font as closed shapes
body:
## What changed

- New module `camcraft_geometry::outline_text`. It reads a TrueType outline font and makes a typed string into closed shapes, in mm, on the layer `text`.
  - `ttf.rs` is our own reader, written from the public OpenType specification. It reads `cmap` formats 4 and 12, `loca`, `glyf` (simple and composite glyphs), `hmtx`, `hhea`, `maxp`, `head` and the `OS/2` cap height. Each read has a bounds check.
  - `mod.rs` flattens the quadratic contours to lines, with a chord error of 0.005 mm or less. It then makes a `SketchData` with closed chains only.
  - `sample_font.rs` makes a small test font in memory. It has our own glyphs, so the repository stores no font file.
- New undoable command `InsertOutlineText` (`crates/app/src/commands/insert_outline_text.rs`). It reads the font once at construction. The profile keeps the shapes, not the font, so the project file format does not change.
- New MCP tool `insert_outline_text` (`crates/app/src/mcp/outline_text_tools.rs`). The tool is also in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (generated) and in the MCP guide table.
- These inputs are refused by name:
  - a font that cannot be read, a CFF font (`.otf` with PostScript outlines) or a font collection;
  - an empty text, or a character that the font does not have;
  - outlines that cross or touch;
  - a nested outline that runs in the same direction as the outline around it (`OutlineTextError::Winding`);
  - a height or a spacing outside the limits;
  - a setup that does not exist, a setup with no stock, or a name that is in use.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3072-outline-text.md`.

## Cause

This is a new feature (#3072). Before this PR, typed text was only single-stroke engraving text (`insert_text`, #2679).

## Review fixes

Round 1:

- Large curves keep the 0.005 mm chord tolerance. A curve can use up to 4096 pieces. A curve that needs more is refused.
- Composite glyphs apply `SCALED_COMPONENT_OFFSET`. A component with both offset flags is refused.
- Table reads use each declared table boundary. Character maps also use each declared subtable boundary.

Round 2:

- Nonzero winding fill. The sketch reads holes by nesting, but a TrueType font fills by the nonzero winding rule. These two readings agree only when each outline runs opposite to the innermost outline around it. `check_winding` in `outline_text/mod.rs` refuses all other arrangements by name. Thus a same-direction inner contour is never made a hole.
- Red verification result. The branch was 106 commits behind `upstream/main`. On the old base, `blind_slot`, `corner_relief_safety` and one post-dialog UI test failed. The trial merge of the reviewer passed them. I merged `upstream/main` into the branch with a merge commit (no rebase, no conflicts). The earlier author run reported a working graphics adapter and a green quick gate on its then-current head. The current round results are below.

Round 3:

- Merged current `upstream/main` `edcbfe4dd678da799d1102cd8324403afaa5c344` with a clean merge commit.
- The GPU bounds loop now iterates over dimensions. This clears the reported upstream `needless_range_loop` warning and preserves every bounds check.
- No UI test was changed or disabled. The current sandbox run cannot find a Metal graphics adapter. No software fallback is available in this build.

## Tests

- Geometry `outline_text`: 10 passed, 0 failed on the final head.
- App `insert_outline_text`: 4 passed, 0 failed on the final head.
- Pin proof, round 2: `nested_outlines_follow_the_nonzero_winding_fill`. With the `check_winding` call removed, the test failed at `crates/geometry/tests/outline_text.rs:233` (the same-direction `O` was accepted). With the call restored, it passed. The test also checks that an `O` with both directions swapped still has one hole, and that `II` stays two shapes.
- Pin proof, round 1: the four round-1 tests failed with the original reviewed source and passed with the fixes:
  - `large_curves_measure_inside_the_chord_tolerance`
  - `composite_offsets_use_the_component_transform`
  - `declared_table_lengths_bound_reads_with_trailing_bytes`
  - `declared_cmap_subtable_lengths_bound_reads`

- Pin proof, round 3: `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with rustc 1.99.1. Restoring the original range loop in the source produced **RED** at `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs:126`. Restoring the fixed dimension iterator in the source produced **GREEN**. The lint command pins this mechanical change.

Final head: `4cc0638eee9155b2cdac957685a0014898caeff3`.
Quick-gate base at start: `upstream/main` `edcbfe4dd678da799d1102cd8324403afaa5c344` (merged into this head).

The shared `upstream/main` reference advanced without our fetch to `b5ef7c39e9504ec67dca67f7727b916550d639d1` before the heavy run. The merge base remains `edcbfe4dd678da799d1102cd8324403afaa5c344`. The tested tree and head did not change during verification. The heavy command uses `--base upstream/main`; its result is below.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **RED**. 1132 steps: 1128 passed, 4 failed, 0 stalled. Wall time: 43.3 minutes.
  - `ui suites: lib`: 1473 passed, 7 failed, 8 ignored.
  - `ui suites: egui_app`: 5 passed, 3 failed.

  - The UI failures report no Metal adapter in this sandbox. This build has no software fallback. Review finding 1 remains unresolved.
  - `app suites: mcp_setup_moves`: `move_an_operation_delete_the_emptied_setup_and_undo_redo_both` failed at line 98. Undo restores setup order as `Front, Back`; the test expects `Back, Front`. This failure is outside the latest review findings. The test and related setup, move and delete command files are identical to upstream. They remain unchanged. No separate upstream baseline run was made.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: **GREEN**. All 251 steps passed. There were 0 failed and 0 stalled steps. Wall time: 31.1 minutes. All four known-fail checks gave the expected results.
- Full gate clippy: **GREEN**. All nine selected crates passed, including GPU, UI, app and geometry. Wall time: 78 seconds. The reported lint in review finding 2 is fixed. Its requirement for a green full quick gate remains unresolved.

- `graphify update`: the command is not installed on this host.

## Overlaps

- #2924 changes `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_tools.rs` (`insert_text`). This PR does not touch that file.

title: feat(post): add the G-EDM 2-axis wire EDM post (g-edm.cps)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/g-edm.cps`, registry name "G-EDM Wire EDM". It serves `wire_edm` machines only. "Generic ISO Wire EDM" stays the default (`WIRE_POSTS[0]`).
- The post writes Grbl-family words only: `G21` / `G20 G90 G17`, `G0` to the threading point, `G1`, `G2` / `G3` with incremental `I J`, and `M30`.
- The post writes no `%` fence, no `O` word, no `F`, no `G40` / `G41` / `G42`, and no work offset word.
- The post reads no `edm.codes`. The condition id is a comment. The header says that the operator sets the spark power at the controller.
- The header has `(NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING)`.
- The post writes one vertical 2-axis wire section for each program.
- These items are refused by name, and no cut is written for the section:
  - a machine that is not `wire_edm`, a rotary, `edm.awt: true`;
  - `WireTaper` not 0, `WireFourAxis`, `WireU` / `WireV`, `WireAngle`;
  - each `COMP` record (G41 / G42);
  - skims;
  - a work offset other than G54;
  - `SpindleSpeed` above 0, `onToolChange`, `onCycle`, a `Z` change;
  - `AfterOperation` `home`, `stop` and `optional-stop`;
  - a second wire section in the same program.
- Registered in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS`) and `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS`, `embedded()`).
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: `WIRE_POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS` name the new post.
- Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, the user guide pages `posting.md` and `machines.md`, and `docs/decisions/2700-g-edm-post.md`.

## Cause

`wire-iso.cps` requires `edm.codes.condition` and `edm.codes.comp_off`, and it writes `%` fences. A G-EDM build sets spark power at the controller and has no condition word. A raw Grbl parser rejects `%`. So no shipped post served a G-EDM build.

## Readings

- #2697 has no new answer from the reporter. The unconfirmed items (`F` and Grbl `error:22`, `G40`, `G54`-`G59`, `M0` pauses, a return move) are not written. The decision file gives the reason for each.
- No `F` word: if G-RBLv3 keeps the Grbl `error:22` check, the controller stops at the first `G1`, before any cut. That is a visible stop, not a wrong cut.
- One section for each program: without a confirmed `M0`, the program cannot stop to cut the wire and thread it again. A `G0` to a second start point would pull the threaded wire through the work.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/app/tests/g_edm_post.rs` (9 tests):

- `g_edm_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate` (golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/wire_slug_punch.nc`, through `posting::post_script`, machine fixture without `edm.codes`)
- `g_edm_post_serves_wire_edms_only_and_is_never_the_default`
- `g_edm_inch_and_arc_words`
- `g_edm_refuses_taper_four_axis_and_lean_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_radius_compensation_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_skims_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_a_mill_machine_and_a_milling_stream_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_what_the_controller_cannot_be_told`
- `g_edm_refuses_a_rapid_with_the_wire_threaded_by_name` (review round 1: a rapid between two cuts refuses by name, and no cut follows it)

Script suite `crates/post/tests/script_g_edm.rs`: 11 recorded streams, each a named refusal (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`).

Red before the fix: all 8 app pins failed with `built-in post G-EDM Wire EDM is not in the registry`.

Mutations (each guard turned off, the pins run, then restored):

- skim guard off: `g_edm_refuses_skims_by_name` red
- `onRadiusCompensation` guard off: `g_edm_refuses_radius_compensation_by_name` red
- one-section guard off: `g_edm_refuses_what_the_controller_cannot_be_told` red
- taper guard off: `g_edm_refuses_taper_four_axis_and_lean_by_name` red
- rapid-while-threaded guard off (`onRapid`, `if (threaded)`): `g_edm_refuses_a_rapid_with_the_wire_threaded_by_name` red
- all restored: 9 of 9 green

Expected change: `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` counts the shipped text posts. After the merge of main (Mach3 added, Agie native refused), the count goes from 21 to 22. `g-edm.cps` passes every per-post check of that test.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `880e5e3d2` (main `f35202134` merged): 797 steps, 0 failed, 1 stalled. The stalled step is `app build (--no-run)`, a cold build after a `cargo clean` with no output for 15 min. Each app suite then built and passed in its own step, `g_edm_post`, `conformance`, `example_catalog` and `mcp_setup_moves` included.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Heavy lanes

Not run, by rule. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) gives no heavy step to a `P2` or lower PR. This PR is `P6`. The full heavy lanes run at the cut, in the cut gate.

None. `app suites: example_catalog` passed on head `880e5e3d2`. The new goldens are only under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/` and `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`. No existing golden changed.

title: feat(cl): translate, XY turn, A/B turn and vertical mirror for toolpaths
body:
## What changed

- A new module `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` with three sub-files (`transform_rotary.rs`, `transform_mirror.rs`, `transform_climb.rs`). `camcraft-app` re-exports it as `app::cl::transform`.
- `translate(tp, [dx, dy, dz])` shifts every move, arc center, canned cycle, compensated span and edge break.
- `transform_xy(tp, tx, ty, angle_deg, pivot)` turns the path in XY about a pivot and then shifts it. Nesting (#2166) can call it directly.
- `rotate_about_axis(tp, RotaryAxis::A | B, origin, angle_deg, chord_tol)` turns the path about X or Y. Each move states the turned tool axis. Arcs become chords within `chord_tol`, or return `ArcChordTolerance`.
- `mirror_plane(tp, MirrorPlane, MirrorMode)` mirrors the path across a vertical plane.
  - `GeometricMirror` gives the exact mirror image: G2 <-> G3 and G41 <-> G42.
  - `PreserveClimb(PassFamily)` mirrors and then runs each pass backwards between its entry and its retract. The lead-out becomes the lead-in. The arcs keep their original G2/G3, and the compensated spans keep their original side.
- `TransformError` names each refusal: `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, `RotaryMove`, `TiltedMove`, `PlasmaCut`, `VerticalArc`, `CannedCycleTilt`, `ArcChordTolerance`, `HorizontalMirrorPlane`, `TiltedMirrorPlane`, `BadInput`, `NotReversible(why)`.
- The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3011-cl-transforms.md`.

## Cause

This is new work. The codebase had no shared transform for toolpaths. Patterns, mirror folders and nesting need one.

## Design

- All four transforms use one map, `p -> M p + t`, with `M` orthogonal.
- An arc keeps its plane only when `M` maps the plane normal exactly onto plus or minus itself. Its turn direction flips when `det(M)` times that sign is negative. This one rule gives the G2/G3 swap under a mirror. It also finds the XZ / YZ arcs that a transform cannot keep.
- Moves, arc centers and cycles snap to the coordinate lattice. Edge-break polylines do not snap, because a snap would move framed caps off orthonormal.
- `PreserveClimb` accepts only contour, profile and chamfer paths. It refuses these by name:
  - a helical ramp, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing and other families;
  - a ramp or helical entry;
  - a level change without a retract;
  - a cut before the first pass or after the last pass;
  - a link that is not on the clearance plane.

## Latest review fix

The latest review found that a collapsed arc could remove a tool axis change. Rounded chord endpoints could match after a preceding move at another pose.

The rotary transform now drops a collapsed chord only when its axis also matches the last emitted pose. It retains a changed axis as a straight move at the standing tip. The move keeps its kind and feed. The same rule retains an initial collapsed arc that states a pose. A distance tolerance cannot permit removal of a required rotation.

## Tests (pins)

The original 20 tests are in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform_tests.rs` and `transform_mirror_tests.rs` (`cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`):

- `translate_shifts_every_record_to_the_micron`, `translate_refuses_a_non_finite_offset`
- `transform_xy_turns_a_quarter_about_the_pivot_then_shifts`, `transform_xy_at_thirty_degrees_is_micron_accurate`, `transform_xy_refuses_a_vertical_arc_it_cannot_keep`
- `rotate_about_a_turns_the_point_and_states_the_axis`, `rotate_about_b_flattens_arcs_within_the_chord_tolerance`, `rotate_about_an_axis_by_zero_is_the_identity`, `rotate_about_an_axis_refuses_a_tilted_canned_cycle`
- `every_transform_refuses_thread_cycles_probe_touches_and_c_moves`
- `geometric_mirror_swaps_g2_g3_and_g41_g42`, `geometric_mirror_on_a_diagonal_plane_is_micron_accurate`, `mirror_refuses_horizontal_and_tilted_planes`, `mirror_refuses_tilted_moves`
- `preserve_climb_reverses_the_pass_between_entry_and_retract`, `preserve_climb_reverses_two_depths_linked_on_the_clearance_plane`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_helical_entry`, `preserve_climb_refuses_clearing_families_by_name`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_cut_before_the_first_pass`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_level_change_without_a_retract`

The initial implementation report states that these pins did not compile before the API existed.

This round adds `rotate_about_a_preserves_the_axis_when_an_arc_collapses`. It checks a short arc after a rapid at another pose. It checks the transformed axis, standing tip, feed, move kind and chain. It also checks the straight-feed control and the unchanged-pose control.

Final head: `91cd4fe1a54a2aae98b95241bbcbbdf563f54c05`.

Pin proof for this round: the verifier saved the fixed rotary source outside the repository. It replaced only that source with the reviewed version from `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`. The new pin stayed in place.

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib rotate_about_a_preserves_the_axis_when_an_arc_collapses -- --nocapture
```

Result: RED, 0 passed and 1 failed. The test expected two moves but received one. The verifier restored the fix and ran:

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform
```

Result: GREEN, all 24 transform tests passed.

## Previous review fix and evidence

The previous review found that the arc sampler stops at 1,024 chords. A 1,000 mm semicircle exceeded the requested 0.0001 mm tolerance.

The rotary transform retains that bounded sampler. It samples at half the requested tolerance. It checks the curve error for the actual chord count and adds the endpoint rounding error. Circular arcs use the sagitta bound. Radius ramps use the sampler's second derivative bound. `ArcChordTolerance` refuses a path when the total bound exceeds `chord_tol`.

That round added these three pins:

- `rotate_about_a_refuses_an_arc_beyond_the_chord_budget`: refuses the review case. It also measures chord midpoint error on an accepted 1,000 mm semicircle.
- `rotate_about_b_bounds_arc_midpoints_in_each_plane`: measures analytic curve midpoint error in XY, XZ and YZ. It covers circular arcs, radius ramps, normal interpolation and both turn directions.
- `rotate_about_a_refuses_rounding_beyond_the_chord_tolerance`: refuses an arc whose endpoint rounding exceeds the tolerance.

Historical proof on `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`: restoring the rotary source from `a273ee018` made two pins fail. The chord-budget and rounding-refusal pins failed. Restoring the fix made all 23 transform tests pass. These results describe the previous round.

The initial implementation report records these mutation results:

- the G2/G3 flip: 3 pins red
- the G41/G42 swap: 2 pins red
- the side restore in the climb reversal: 1 pin red
- the probe refusal: 1 pin red
- the refusal of a cut before the first pass: 1 pin red
- the horizontal-plane refusal: 1 pin red
- the pass reversal: 2 pins red
- the tilted-cycle refusal: 1 pin red

## Final validation

Validation head: `91cd4fe1a54a2aae98b95241bbcbbdf563f54c05`.

Quick base: `60376ccbbfa52305db6fa880278222e7854fcdbf` (`upstream/main` at quick start).

Heavy base: `edcbfe4dd678da799d1102cd8324403afaa5c344` (`upstream/main` at heavy start). Another session advanced the shared ref before heavy started.

Both bases have merge base `d911f45535df24c42d5fde5feaed386c5fca4907` with this head. The selected eight-file diff is unchanged. The commands test the PR head directly. No trial merge was tested.

- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`: GREEN, 24 passed after restoration.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,077 steps, 0 failed, 20.9 minutes.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, 0.87 seconds. The quick gate also passed clippy for all selected crates, with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`, in 37 seconds.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 241 steps, 0 failed, 42.9 minutes. Registered known-fail checks matched their expected results.
- `app suites: example_catalog`: GREEN, 34 passed and 4 ignored.
- `app heavy: example_catalog`: GREEN, the remaining 4 passed. All 38 catalog cases passed across the debug and heavy steps.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive` and `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: GREEN, 1 passed each.
- `app suites: golden_cl`: GREEN, 33 passed.
- `git diff --check`: GREEN. The tracked worktree is clean at the final head.

UI screenshots: not applicable. This PR changes no UI code or assets.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog and reached golden suites ran. No recorded program changed or required regeneration.

## Not exercised

- No caller exists yet: patterns, mirror folders and nesting (#2166) will use it.
- No posted G-code goes through a transformed path in this PR.
- The framed edge-break caps under a turn and under a mirror are not pinned by a test.
- Integration with the current `upstream/main` was not tested. These runs test the PR head directly.

## Overlaps

#3046 adds a line to the module list of `crates/cl/src/cl/mod.rs`. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Fixes #3011

title: feat(post): add RichAuto DSP A11 3-axis router post (.mmg format)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/richauto.cps` for the RichAuto DSP A11 router controller.
- The post is registered as `"RichAuto DSP A11"` in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`). It comes after Mach4, before Mach3.
- The output follows the `.mmg` program that a Laguna Swift A11 runs (#1907, comment of 2026-11-18). The comment of 2026-11-18 on this issue names that program as the conformance target.
  - The file extension is `.mmg`.
  - Each block has a sequence number: `N10`, then steps of 10. Comment lines and the `%` line have no number.
  - There are no spaces between words.
  - Lengths have three decimals. `F` is mm/min with one decimal.
  - Rapid is `G00` and feed is `G1`. The spindle starts with `M03S<rpm>` and stops with `M05`.
  - An axis word or an `F` word that does not change is not written.
  - The program ends with `M30` and then a `%` line.
- The setup block is `G21G90G17`. The post writes no `G54`, `G40`, `G80`, `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, `G49`, `T` or `M6` word.
- Offset 1 is the work origin that the operator sets on the pendant. Offsets 2 and higher are refused by name.
- Arcs use incremental `I`/`J`/`K` (`AbsCntr = Off`). An arc of more than 180 degrees is split.
- Drilling cycles are expanded to plain `G00`/`G1` moves, with the floor dwell and the bore spindle stop and restart.
- The `SpindleDwellMs` option writes `G04P<ms>` after the spindle start. The default is 0.
- The post refuses these by name: tapping, `G41`/`G42`, probing, rotary moves, `G96`, a second tool, an inch document, a bad rpm, a bad coolant, and a missing or low clearance plane.
- The post writes header notes (#2996) and WARN records as `(...)` comments.

## Cause

The shipped posts do not run safely on an A11. They write `G91.1`, `G53`, `T.. M6`, `G43` and canned cycles. A basic A11 firmware can refuse these words.

## Tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_richauto.rs` and `crates/post/tests/richauto_safety/mod.rs`: 42 tests, including the 11 recorded-stream goldens of `post_suite!`.
- The pin `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format` was red on the older held script (format without `N`, `%`): `the program ends with %`. It is green on the new script.
- On `upstream/main` all the pins are red, because the post does not exist.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: RichAuto is added to `POSTS`, `REFUSED` (`tap_plate`, "tapping"), the synth stream (G54, no tap) and `EXTENSIONS` (`mmg`). All 7 tests pass.
- `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`: 22 text posts write both header notes. The native Agie dispatcher refuses them by name.
- Mutations. Each mutant was run against the pins, then the script was restored and the pins were green again:
  - no final `%` line: 8 tests red, including `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format`;
  - spaces between words: 18 tests red;
  - no modal word omission: 11 tests red, including `unchanged_axis_and_feed_words_are_left_out`;
  - no `onComment` hook: `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` red;
  - no sequence step (all blocks `N0`): 7 tests red.
- The earlier coolant fix retains operation names in every coolant refusal. The pin is `richauto_safety::coolant_refusals_name_the_operation`.

## Author refresh and final-head verification

The refresh merges `upstream/main` at `35e3bd173d084c73c6fb3e6819a0247b7060dcb5`.
It keeps both RichAuto and Mach3 registry entries, embedded scripts, conformance cases and extensions.
It keeps the separate text-post and native-refusal counters and all comment assertions.
It also imports the upstream correction for `slot_dxf_outline.cl`, identified in #3293 through `f4b351682` and PR #3285.

Final head: `e276e36058733af7c0fae58bffaa8898bbb16922`.

The first quick run passed 794 of 795 steps on the earlier merge head.
The only failure was `app suites: mcp_setup_moves`. Its isolated repeat passed 0 of 1 steps.
That test still expected name order after undo, although upstream now uses creation order.
This refresh also imports upstream commit `1c6002baa313f0f31643acca790ea281fe929406` through PR #3603.
The upstream test now captures the setup list before deletion and checks both undo operations against that list.
Final verification on the new merge head passes as recorded below.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **GREEN: 795 of 795 steps passed, 0 failed; 48.3 minutes**.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: **GREEN: 212 of 212 steps passed, 0 failed; 31.4 minutes**. Selected lanes: **app heavy: every target**.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **passed: `cargo clippy -j24 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` (1 minute 6 seconds)**.
- Catalog and reached golden suites: **All passed in the final quick gate: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `conformance`, `recorded_streams`, `solid_law_goldens` and `slot_dxf_sketch`**.
- Pin proof: **The old slot golden, the omitted RichAuto registry entry and the text-post count changed from 22 to 21 each made its pin fail (RED, exit 101). Restoring each fix made its pin pass (GREEN, exit 0)**. The slot pin is `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size`.
- Registry pin: `conformance::every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles`.
- Extension pin: `conformance::every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`.
- Comment pin: `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound`.
- No UI changes are in this fix round. Screenshots do not apply.

## Goldens moved

No existing PR golden changed relative to the current upstream base.
The refresh imports `crates/app/tests/golden/slot_dxf_outline.cl` from upstream.
That upstream fix generated the v2 record with 15 moves, replacing the stale v1 record with 9 moves.
This round does not regenerate that file locally because the upstream commit already supplies the generated correction.
**The final quick gate passed the catalog and reached golden suites. No golden file changed during the tests**.

The original RichAuto additions remain unchanged. These 24 files pin the new post and its refusals:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/richauto/contour_disc_hole.nc`.

title: fix(post): block cutting tools at reserved numbers and names
body:
## What changed

Machine files accept `tooling.reserved` entries.
Each entry reserves a number, a name, or both for `probe` or `tool_setter`.
The reader and validator refuse malformed entries by key.
Stored projects retain the reservations.

New cutting tools skip reserved numbers.
A probe takes a declared probe pocket.
Tool edits and library imports refuse incompatible reserved numbers or names.
Verification and posting also refuse old unsafe assignments.
The existing GUI, script, and MCP commands use these checks.
Tool number zero remains refused.

The standalone post CLI checks its input before it creates or replaces output.
It retains the loaded tool across sections.
A new TOOL needs its own declared kind.
A stream with no tool selector cannot post motion on a machine with reservations.
Indexed lookups keep the checks bounded for long streams.

A machine that omits the field reserves nothing.
No shipped machine file reserves a pocket in this PR (see "Review round 2").

### Project file version 78 (breaking)

A stored machine can hold `reserved_tools`. `PROJECT_VERSION` steps from 77 to 78.
An older reader refuses a v78 file. It cannot drop the reservation and post a cutting tool at a reserved pocket.
The step is a pure step-up: a v77 file opens with no change.
The rule entries are in `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` and `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs`.

PR #3485 merged first and took 77 for the setup `order` key (#3447). This PR takes 78.
Main's v77 meaning is unchanged.

This is a breaking change of the project file.
Commit `8f541fdc3` is `fix(project)!:` and has the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

## Cause

Tool allocation considered only document numbers.
Machine files could not protect a probe pocket or a control-managed tool name.
The app and standalone post paths had no reservation check.

## Review round 2 (second review of `e6881bb0a`)

- Blocker, version step: done (above).
- T99 provenance: removed. I found no public Tormach document that names T99 as the probe pocket.
  The earlier #362 research calls T99 a convention of the PathPilot probing screens only.
  The 18 Tormach files are identical to `main` again. A follow-up can add T99 with a cited document.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`: the `tooling.reserved` row is added.
- MCP text: the `add_tool` description now says that the number skips the machine's reservations.
  It changes in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`.
- Body: refreshed. Parent #3157 merged, so the stack note and the parent's screenshots are removed.

## Review round 3 (review of `3b5f359ff`)

- Version step: now 78. The constant, the rule entries, the pins, the fixture and the decision say 78.
- NEW blocker, breaking-change marker: commit `8f541fdc3` has the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. The history is kept.
- Conflict with `main`: I merged `upstream/main` at `f2b2369ed` with a merge commit (`23685c1c7`).
  - `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` and `apply.rs`: the two sides stay. Main's v77 entry comes first, then the v78 entry of this PR.
  - `crates/app/tests/deburr_chord_width.rs`: main's side is taken. It has the same intent as the earlier change of this PR.

## Screenshots

This PR changes no UI file. No screenshot applies.

## Tests on the final head

Final head: `8f541fdc3`. Base: `upstream/main` at `f2b2369ed` (merged into the branch).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 160 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 5.2 min |
| `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` | 3 steps, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | passed |
| `example_catalog` | 37 passed, 4 ignored |

Heavy lanes: not run on this head. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) gives a P6 PR no heavy step.
The reviewer ran the heavy gate on `3b5f359ff`: 212 steps, 0 failed.

### Pins and mutation proof (rounds 2 and 3)

| Pin | Mutation | Mutated | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| `saved_machine_reservations_need_the_v78_reader` (`crates/app/tests/tool_reservations_version.rs`) | `PROJECT_VERSION` back to 77 | RED at line 26 | GREEN |

title: feat(multiaxis): Multi-Axis Deburr - tilted chamfer-mill edge breaks with holder tilt-away
body:
## Second-review fixes (current round)

Final head: `fdb1630fef05fb9b46d20a1673e5e8540ae69a12`. These fixes answer the review on head `ebe55a46f`.

1. **Posted golden and the two rotary laws.** New suite `crates/app/tests/mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post.rs`. It posts three sections on the tilt head with the Fanuc post: an upright Deburr, the Multi-Axis Deburr, and an upright Deburr after it.
   - `the_three_section_tilthead_program_matches_its_golden` locks the program in `golden/nc/multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc`: retract, turn, approach, cut, retract, return.
   - `the_tilted_section_states_its_rotary_pose_before_its_first_tilted_feed` pins #3421. A rapid states A and B before the first tilted feed. The stated pose is the pose of that feed. No feed turns a rotary on the way in.
   - `the_upright_section_after_the_tilted_section_returns_the_rotaries_first` pins #3478. The tilted section ends leaned. The next section commands A0 and B0 after `G28`, before its first X/Y traverse.
   - The tilted window stops at Z 9 in this fixture. The top edges are outside it, so every pose leans and the section ends leaned. With the full window the last pose is upright, and the return law has nothing to test.
2. **The shank toggle.** The page no longer shows "Avoid shank collisions" for this kind. It shows a read-only row "Shank and holder guard: Always on" with a true hint. The `shank_avoid` field stays in the file and MCP grammar and has no effect. Decision: `docs/decisions/1894-multiaxis-deburr.md`. Pin: `egui_app::tests::ma_deburr_page::the_passes_tab_shows_the_shank_guard_as_always_on_with_no_switch`.
3. **The setup law on the page.** The Geometry tab shows one visible line: the stock must be the source model, and the setup can hold no other part. Pin: `egui_app::tests::ma_deburr_page::the_geometry_tab_states_the_stock_and_part_law`.
4. **One `Changelog:` line.** The body now has one line, at the end.
5. **`Axis4` posted.** `axis4_posts_with_the_a_axis_only` posts `Axis4` with a 60-degree cone on the tilt head. A turns on the top edges along X. B stays zero in the whole program.

Pin proof (each mutation was reverted after the run):

- `uprightAfterTilt()` in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` returns at once: the return pin and the golden go red.
- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` writes no angles on a leaned rapid: the pose pin, the return pin and the golden go red.
- `kernel_params` reads `Axis4` as `Axis5`: the `Axis4` test goes red. The post refuses the program first (a crossing finding), before the B check.
- The page source of `ebe55a46f`: both `ma_deburr_page` tests go red.

The branch merges `upstream/main` two times in this round, at `b5ef7c39e` and then `f35202134`. Both merges were clean, with no hand edits. The first merge brings the #3478 post fix that the return pin needs. The second brings main's fix of `mcp_setup_moves` (`1c6002baa`). That suite failed in the first gate run of this round, and it failed on main too (#3606).

Gates on the final head `fdb1630fe` (main merged at `f35202134`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 762 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 73.2 minutes. It includes `mcp_multiaxis_deburr` (9), `mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post` (4), `mcp_setup_moves`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and the UI library.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on `fdb1630fe` (run after the push, no new commit): 253 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 35.6 minutes. Lanes `motion heavy` and `app heavy`; the four known-fail checks (#1950, #2849) were red as expected.
- Trial merge of `fdb1630fe` with main `1e7800a9e` (local, not pushed; clean, no hand edits): motion lib deburr tests 13, `mcp_multiaxis_deburr` 9, `mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post` 4, `operations` 121, `ribbon` 13 and the UI page tests 3 pass.
- Goldens: one new posted golden (see "Goldens moved"). No existing recorded program or catalog program changed.

Screenshots (rendered by the app's own UI test harness, `Harness::render`, on the same page fixture as the pins). They are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `76aa2020acf66b2ae4a63d450cb63605b1b4c4b8`.

| Before (`ebe55a46`) | After (`fdb1630f`) |
|---|---|
| ![Before: Passes page with the shank check box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/76aa2020acf66b2ae4a63d450cb63605b1b4c4b8/pr-3283/before-passes-ebe55a46.png) | ![After: Passes page with the guard shown as always on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/76aa2020acf66b2ae4a63d450cb63605b1b4c4b8/pr-3283/after-passes-fdb1630f.png) |
| ![Before: Geometry page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/76aa2020acf66b2ae4a63d450cb63605b1b4c4b8/pr-3283/before-geometry-ebe55a46.png) | ![After: Geometry page with the stock and part line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/76aa2020acf66b2ae4a63d450cb63605b1b4c4b8/pr-3283/after-geometry-fdb1630f.png) |

## Stock safety fix (earlier round)

Final head: `ebe55a46f01c774fbdcdcdd49f05205cfb8ec550`.

Multi-Axis Deburr now requires the complete stock boundary to match the source mesh.
Generation and posting refuse missing, empty, non-finite or different stock by name.
The comparison sorts triangle vertices and triangles. It ignores ordering, normals and winding.
Equal bounds do not satisfy the check.

For matching stock, the existing source guard checks the cone, flute, shank and holder through the cut, entry and exit.
Generation also runs the shared `plunge_solid::audit_posed` check.
Posting reads the live stock before it accepts a cached path.
The refusal also applies to a safe different tessellation or stock removed by an earlier operation.
The column simulator still does not judge posed moves. The named refusal prevents an unproved stock verdict from permitting posting.

Pins in `mcp_multiaxis_deburr`:

- `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_stock_beside_the_vertical_edge`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_rechecks_stock_before_posting_the_cached_path`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_live_stock_judge_refuses_an_unjudged_cached_path`.

The clear controls first generate and post source-shaped stock.
The unsafe case adds 60 x 60 x 10 mm stock beside a 40 x 40 x 10 mm part.
The generation pin also sets `center_cutting=true` to isolate the complete-tool guard from the plunge check.
The cached-post pin checks the actual post command after a stock edit. Freshness refuses it and no NC file is written.
The direct live-judge pin checks the named stock refusal independently of freshness.

Pin proof:

- Removing only the generation stock guard makes `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_stock_beside_the_vertical_edge` fail. Generation returns `status: ok`.
- Removing only the live stock guard makes `multiaxis_deburr_live_stock_judge_refuses_an_unjudged_cached_path` fail. The judge returns `None`.
- Restoring both source files byte for byte makes all nine `mcp_multiaxis_deburr` tests pass.

`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_multiaxis_deburr` passed all nine tests on the final head.

Final-head quick gate:

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 526 steps in 75.3 minutes.
The run had zero failures and zero stalls. It used the merged main revision `deb5364ee`.
Motion library: 551 passed, 10 ignored. App library: 297 passed.
UI library: 1434 passed, 8 ignored. MCP suite: nine passed.
`slot_dxf_sketch`: four passed. No reached golden changed.
The shared `upstream/main` reference advanced to `ef157211` during the run. The tested tree did not change.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final head in 1 minute 31 seconds.

Final-head heavy gate:

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 244 steps in 58.4 minutes.
The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. The run had zero failures and zero stalls.
All 108 ordinary ignored tests passed. All four known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
The heavy `example_catalog` suite passed all four tests.
The command used the current `upstream/main` reference after its advance to `ef157211`.
The tested head remained `ebe55a46f01c774fbdcdcdd49f05205cfb8ec550`.

Catalog and goldens on the final head:

- `app suites: example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored, zero failures.

## Separate-part safety fix (earlier round)

Head: `91a03dd8c9d000effb3f4510bd325495a6d22d05`.

Multi-Axis Deburr now refuses by name when another kept part exists. Generation collects the other parts through the shared keep law. Posting checks the live parts before it accepts a cached path. - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 242/242 passed. Reached lanes: `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. All 102 ordinary ignored tests passed. All six expected-failure checks matched.

## What changed

- A new operation kind, **Multi-Axis Deburr** (`OpType::MultiAxisDeburr`), is appended at ordinal 46 in `Section::MultiAxis`. Stored kind ids do not move.
- It has every field of the 3D Deburr and five more: `axis_mode` (`Axis5` / `Axis4`), `lead_deg`, `lag_deg`, `max_tilt_deg` and `shank_avoid`.
- New kernel `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::multiaxis_deburr` (`deburr_axis.rs`, `deburr_pose.rs`):
  - The tool lays one cone flank on the chamfer plane of each break. The cut is the flat chamfer for every pose that turns the axis about the plane normal.
  - `Axis5` leans the axis inside `max_tilt_deg`. `Axis4` keeps the axis square to the A axis (about X).
  - Mandatory continuous facet checks cover the full cone and the supplied physical shank and holder. They cover each complete cut, entry and exit. The stored `shank_avoid` option cannot disable this guard.
  - An edge with no clear pose follows the Deburr's unreachable-edge policy: skip with a note, or refuse by name.
  - The tool enters and leaves along a checked, bounded axis line. The entire cone stays above `bottom_z`. Pose changes, gaps and chamfer-plane corners split runs.
  - Each run declares a framed flat `EdgeBreak` cap (#1891).
- The exposed-edge scan moved from `finishing3d/deburr.rs` into the shared `finishing3d/deburr_scan.rs`. The 3D Deburr calls it in the same order.
- App wiring: kind row, seed, sanity door (lead minus lag inside the cap), generate arm, cache stamp, project DTO (`multi_axis_deburr`), heights, setup sheet, section mode, WCS refusals, sim break bound.
- MCP: `add_operation`, `edit_operation` and `set_operation_geometry` work with the new kind through the generic tools.
- UI: `multiaxis_deburr_page.rs` (Geometry: size, filters, unreachable policy; Passes: axis mode, lean, max tilt, shank avoid; Heights; Feeds). The kind has its own original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-multiaxis-deburr.svg`, PNG from `cargo xtask icons`).

## Cause

New feature (#1894). A vertical cone cannot break steep or vertical edges, so the 3D Deburr skips them.

title: feat(post): ship an example starter set on the Sodick ALC400G
body:
## What changed

- `assets/machines/sodick-alc400g.mch` now states an example starter set:
  - three conditions for a 0.25 mm wire: `C110` rough (gap 0.04 mm), `C120` skim (gap 0.02 mm), `C130` finish (gap 0.01 mm);
  - `edm.lower_guide_z` 0 and `edm.upper_guide_z` 130 mm;
  - `edm.awt: true`.
- Each condition's `notes` says "EXAMPLE - not a Sodick figure; replace with the row of your control's condition table". The file description says the same for the whole set.
- The EDM guide page (`operations-edm.md`) gives the steps to replace the examples. `machines.md` and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` describe the starter set.
- `docs/decisions/3214-sodick-starter-conditions.md` records the choices.

## Cause

The built-in machine stated no condition, no guide heights and no threader. Each Wire Contour was refused until the user wrote a `.mch` file.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/app/tests/sodick_alc400g.rs`:

- `the_shipped_starter_set_is_marked_as_examples_to_replace` (new): the conditions, guide heights and AWT are stated, each id is `C` and three digits, each row and the description say EXAMPLE.
- `a_first_wire_contour_generates_and_posts_on_the_shipped_file` (replaces `the_shipped_file_refuses_a_cut_until_the_user_states_a_condition`): a punch on `C110` generates and posts on the unchanged shipped file. The program has `C110`, `T91` and `T90`.
- `a_punch_posts_through_the_sodick_post_on_it` (changed): the user replaces the table with `C210`. The punch posts on `C210`. A punch on the removed `C110` is refused by name.
- `a_tapered_punch_is_refused_at_post_while_the_file_states_no_guide_heights` (changed): on the shipped file the door admits 5 deg and the Sodick post refuses it ("is tapered - ... vertical 2-axis cut only"). With the guide heights removed, the two guide-height refusals stay pinned.

Red before the fix: yes. Three pins failed on the old file ("machine Sodick ALC400G states no EDM condition \"C110\"", "edm.conditions is stated").

Mutation: the old `.mch` put back gives the same three failures. The new file gives 6 passed.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (app `sodick_alc400g`, `probe_no_coolant`; post `machine_tree`, `ream_lathe`).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test machine --test posting --test machine_library`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No real Sodick control. The example values are not Sodick figures.
- The MCP `add_operation` path was not run. It uses the same `CreateOperation` door that the pins use.
- No default condition is picked for a new Wire Contour. The user still names one; the refusal lists the machine's conditions. #3183 covers conditions from the machine's own table.

## Overlaps

These PRs touch the same files, in different functions or lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.

- `crates/app/tests/sodick_alc400g.rs`: #2972, #2974, #2978, #2979, #2981, #2992, #2993, #2999 add fields to the `WireContourOp` literal in `punch_world`. This PR does not change that literal.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`: #3157 (line 40), #3204 (line 285). This PR changes the EDM paragraphs near lines 94 and 104.
- `site/content/guide/operations/operations-edm.md`: #3162 (lines 58, 283, 348). This PR changes lines 17-20 and the Conditions paragraph.

Changelog: The built-in Sodick ALC400G ships an example starter set (conditions C110 / C120 / C130, guide heights, automatic threading), so a first Wire Contour generates and posts; replace the examples with your control's table (#3214).

## Review round 2 (head `0c58a2032`)

- The Sodick post writes the kerf gap of each posted condition as a program note. An `EXAMPLE` row gets a WARNING note that names the example gap. The wire machine mirror now sends `edm.conditions` when the file has a table.
- Pins: `sodick_alc400g::a_first_wire_contour_generates_and_posts_on_the_shipped_file` (WARNING note for C110) and `sodick_alc400g::a_punch_posts_through_the_sodick_post_on_it` (gap note for C210, no `EXAMPLE` text). Both fail without the fix and pass with it.
- Goldens moved (note lines only, no motion change): the four `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/*.nc` programs. Reason: the new gap note.
- Quick gate: 73 steps, 0 failed. Heavy (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 199 steps, 0 failed. `example_catalog`: 33 passed. Clippy (app, post): clean.
- Changelog addition: The Sodick wire post states the kerf gap of each condition and warns on an example condition row.

Fixes #3214

title: feat(import): state the STEP length unit, and ask for it when the file has none
body: ## What changed A STEP model import states the length unit that the model was read in. A STEP file that states no length unit is never read in a guessed unit. - **Kernel** (`crates/kernel/src/step_assumed_unit.rs`, `solidcore_step.rs`, `solidcore_step_import.rs`): `read_step_assuming` and `import_step_model_assuming` take the caller's millimetres per unit. For a file whose contexts state no length unit, the unit is written into each representation context before the read. The tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord are then in the same unit as the geometry. A file that states its own unit keeps it. A stated size outside 0.001..=1000 mm is refused by name. - **Geometry** (`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`): `parse_open_assuming`. A file with no length unit and no caller unit is `StepError::MissingUnits`. `StepMesh` carries `length_units_mm` and `assumed_mm`. - **App**: - `ImportError::StepUnitsMissing`. - `ImportModel::within_in` and `from_bytes_in`, and the unit option on each import path: the file, the bytes, the sourced load and the cadmpeg conversion. - A unit for a file that is not STEP is refused by name before parsing, as a facet budget is. - The last import note names the unit: `length unit: in (stated by the file)`, `length unit: in (stated at import; the file states no length unit)`, or `... (stated by the file; the in stated at import is not used)`. - **MCP and script**: `import_model` takes `units` (`"mm"` or `"in"`). `cam.import` takes it as the fourth argument. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are regenerated. - **UI**: a refused unitless import opens the **Length unit** modal (`egui_app/step_units_prompt.rs`), with the buttons Millimeters (mm), Inches (in) and Cancel. The answer goes through the command queue (`CommandKind::ResolveStepUnits`) and runs the same import again. The import that lands is one undoable command. Cancel and Escape import nothing. An import-as-fixture binding is kept for the second import. - **Docs**: `units-and-coordinates.md` (it said that a unitless STEP file "is kept as millimetres") and a new `troubleshooting.md` entry. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1874-step-length-units.md`. ## Screenshot The Length unit prompt for a STEP file that states no length unit (the status line under it says the same): ## Decisions (see the decision record) - The file's own unit wins over the caller's (the DXF import does the reverse, #1862). A STEP unit context is an exact statement of the CAD system. - The chosen unit is not recorded on the model. title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

The SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads drawings into the DXF `Document` type. It shares sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, sketch entities, and project storage with DXF import.

- Read paths, lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, and ellipses.
- Apply group transforms and references to elements in the same file.
- Keep circular arcs analytic. Flatten Beziers and other ellipses within 0.005 mm.
- Read mm, cm, in, pt, pc, and px sizes, `viewBox`, and `preserveAspectRatio`.
- Reflect Y about the page height. Use top-level group labels or IDs as layers.
- Count unsupported content, hidden content, and stylesheets as skipped. This includes stylesheets inside `<defs>`.
- Add the undoable `ImportSvg` command, the `import_svg` MCP tool, and the `cam.importSvg` script verb.
- Update the user guide and MCP reference. Record decisions in `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals

The reader names malformed input, unsupported units, invalid sizes, singular transforms, and exceeded import limits. A file without physical units needs the caller's unit. A sized file refuses a caller unit.

The reader also refuses inline CSS `transform` declarations and root `<svg>` transform attributes.

This review fix refuses `transform-origin` presentation attributes and inline CSS declarations by name before drawing geometry. Pins cover both sources.

## Validation on the final head

Head: `ad6709150d06595bc5b347a651702854681f457c`.
Base at gate launch: `upstream/main`, `6e641dac753020bfed49fec310237eed28448141`.
Upstream advanced during the run to `64b7377297c95d1614c93835c1a1bef18c6de174`.
The gates tested the final PR head. They did not test a trial merge.
A merge-tree check with the newer upstream head is clean.
Selection comparison against the newer base: the old and current bases have the same merge base, `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`. Quick (1,067 steps) and heavy (241 steps) select identical step names and commands against both bases. The final source and selection are unchanged, so no rerun was required.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 1,067 steps, zero failures, 40.8 minutes |
| `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 241 steps, zero failures, 65.1 minutes |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS in the final quick gate; all targets with `-D warnings`, including geometry, app, and six other crates |
| `app suites: example_catalog` | `app suites: example_catalog` in the final quick gate: 33 passed, 2 ignored; adaptive and edgework catalog suites: 1 passed each |
| SVG suites and other reached golden suites | SVG: 15 passed; refusals: 16 passed; visibility: 11 passed. Total: 42 passed. Reached catalog suites passed |

Pin proof:

- `svg_transform_origin_attribute_is_refused_by_name`: removing the attribute guard failed the exact pin at its assertion (exit 101); restoring the guard passed the pin (1 passed).
- `svg_inline_css_transform_origin_is_refused_by_name`: removing the inline guard failed the exact pin at its assertion (exit 101); restoring the guard passed the pin (1 passed).

Each mutation removed the relevant refusal, failed the pin, restored the refusal, and passed the pin.

An earlier seeded run failed with an infrastructure error (`E0463`) in the kernel artifact cache. A targeted repair restored the cache. The final quick gate above passed without seed artifacts.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog suites passed. No recorded program or golden changed, so no regeneration was required.

- A posted G-code golden for an SVG profile remains in follow-up #3042. This fix round did not exercise it.
- The `import_svg` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` remains outside this fix round.
- Nested SVG viewports, stylesheet evaluation, text to outlines, and embedded images remain outside this reader's scope.

No UI source changed. Before/after screenshots do not apply.

title: feat(waterjet): Waterjet Profile operation on a shared 2D sheet kernel
body:
## What changed

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/sheet/`).** The kernel code moves out of `plasma` and `wire_edm` without a change of behaviour:
  - `nest` (contour roles, inner-first cut order) and `ring` (kerf ring, walks), from `plasma`;
  - `laws` (kerf law, cover law) and `lead` (straight and arc leads), from `plasma`;
  - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), from `wire_edm::tabs`;
  - `open` (the one-sided offset of an open run), from `wire_edm::open`.

  A `Voice` keeps each refusal text word for word. Plasma and wire EDM now call the shared code.
- **Cover law.** The law now takes one span or more for each contour, and an `exempt` closure for a tab's bridge. Plasma exempts no point. The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
- **Waterjet generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`).** `waterjet_profile` does these steps:
  - It cuts the inner contours first, with the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side.
  - It adds straight or arc leads, with the pierce in the scrap. A lead with no room is halved up to four times.
  - It pierces a tight hole at its centre when the lead has no room after the halving.
  - It cuts tabs as uncut gaps. Each stretch between two gaps gets its own pierce, lead-in and lead-out.
  - It cuts open runs on the centre line, or to the left or right of travel.
  - It can post G41/G42, and it can send arcs as chords (`Move::chords`).

  The kerf law and the cover law certify the result.
- **App.** The changes are:
  - `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (stored id 46; main holds 44 for Slot Undercut and 45 for V-Carve), `Section::Waterjet` and `Family::Waterjet`. The op mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet` nozzle only.
  - `WaterjetOp` with its command-door sanity check, `waterjet_op.rs` (seed, params, generate) and the digest bytes.
  - A `.camproj` DTO (`waterjet_profile`, additive).
  - Each exhaustive match in the app gets a waterjet arm.
  - Profile (DXF) sources are admitted. The family door has its own words: "mount a waterjet first".
  - MCP reaches the kind through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`. The `add_operation` text now names waterjet.
- **UI.** The changes are:
  - `waterjet_page.rs` with these fields: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side, send arcs as lines, sheet heights, tabs, lead shape and lengths, cut feed, pierce time, abrasive delay. It has no torch height or THC field.
  - The Waterjet ribbon section.
  - An original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-waterjet-profile.svg`, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`).

## Readings

- Golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` has 149 moves, 5 pierces and 3 holes cut before the outline. The outline is cut as two led-in stretches between 2 mm tabs.
- The existing goldens do not change. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows only the new file. The plasma golden `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl` stays byte-identical after the kernel move.

## Goldens moved

- `crates/app/tests/golden/waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl`: **new file**. It records the first waterjet program: a plate with three holes and two tabs on the outline. The holes are cut before the outline. Each pierce is in the scrap. The kerf ring is 0.4 mm on the waste side. No existing recorded program changes.
- Run on the final head `e85e4a88b`: `golden_cl` (34 passed), `example_catalog` (37 passed, 4 ignored in debug), `example_catalog_adaptive` (1 passed), `example_catalog_edge_work` (1 passed). `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/catalog` shows only the new file.

## Tests (pins)

Each pin was red before this change: the module and the kind did not exist, so the pins could not compile.

- motion `waterjet::tests` (9): `holes_are_cut_before_the_outline_and_every_pierce_is_in_the_waste`, `straight_leads_lay_no_arc_on_a_square_part`, `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_and_each_stretch_is_pierced_and_led_in`, `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre`, `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords`, `an_open_run_rides_its_stated_side`, `control_compensation_records_a_comp_span_per_untabbed_contour`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`.
- app `waterjet_profile` (6): the family door, hole first, tabs, a milling tool refused, create / edit / undo / redo, and a byte-identical `.camproj` round trip.
- app `mcp_waterjet` (1): add, edit, undo, redo and generate over MCP.
- app `golden_cl::waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes_matches_golden`.
- ui `waterjet_ribbon_tests` (2): the section shows on a waterjet only, the tip names the waterjet, the glyph is its own, and the page has a leads tab.
- Plasma and wire EDM: all `camcraft-motion` plasma, sheet and wire tests pass, and all 34 `golden_cl` tests pass.

## Mutation results

Each mutation was applied, the pins were run, and then the code was restored (green again).

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Inner-first order removed | red: `holes_are_cut_before_...`, `a_tight_hole_...` |
| Tabs ignored | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...`, `bad_input_...` |
| Tight-hole rule off | red: `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre` |
| Linearization ignored | red: `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords` |
| Cover law exempts every point | red: `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` |
| Cover law exempts no point | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...` (6 mm tabs) |
| Leads on the part side | red: 7 of 9 pins |

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 422 steps ran (374 app, 44 post, 3 motion, 1 cl). The only red steps were kind-count pins that this change extends on purpose: `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`, `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` and `tests/ribbon.rs` (`family_is_derived_not_forked`, `the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`). I updated them to 45 kinds and the Waterjet section. Because I edited during the run, the gate marked that run VOID. `--failed` on the committed tree then ran the red step: green. The app lib suite is green (290).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1324 passed, 0 failed. The waterjet row was added to `tips_match_the_imgui_table`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

- Review fix on `aded58c47` (merged with `upstream/main` `f036dddad`):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 694 steps, 1 failed. The red step is `app suites: tool_gate` (`the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry`). Its red row is `OpType::Finish3D`: `upstream/main` (#3069) adds `Router ball nose 6 mm` before `BN-0600` in the catalog, and the tie goes to the first entry. The step is red on `upstream/main` too. The waterjet row in the same test passes.
  - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 237 steps, 0 failed. The lanes are `motion heavy` (37 steps), `app heavy` (199 steps) and the heavy build.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

- Review fix on `aded58c47`, round 3. The final head is `e85e4a88b`, merged with `upstream/main` `f35202134`:
  - The merge resolved 17 conflicts by hand and kept both sides in each hunk. `job.rs` keeps main's `wire_sketch.is_none()` guard and adds the waterjet arm. Waterjet Profile moved to the free stored id 46. `pick_kinds.rs` (new on main) gives it `PICK_OWED`, as for plasma.
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 742 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (48.1 min).
  - `the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry` passes. Main fixed the Finish3D row in `3f945362a` (the size tie now breaks by name).
  - Stored id pin: `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input`. Mutation: id 44 for Waterjet gives RED ("row 46 out of step with ordinal"). The restored id 46 gives GREEN.
  - `cargo xtask gate light`: 3 steps, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.
  - The full heavy lanes did not run again for this round. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) retires them at review: they run at the cut. This PR is P4, so no targeted heavy step applies. The last heavy run on `aded58c47` had 237 steps and 0 failed.

## Not exercised

- Posting. No post serves `Kind::Waterjet` yet. The pierce time and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only. #1882 adds the CL record and the post hooks.
- `verify` and the post gate for a waterjet op. That is #1885.

No merge or push occurred. No programs or goldens changed. No source fix was made, so no new pin or mutation check applies. There is no UI change that requires screenshots.

The draft status and review labels remain unchanged. The warm worktree remains in place. The results below describe earlier rounds.

## Review fixes and final-head validation

Final head: `e302dc0f000ecde4f2a52ddb63fb9879b6004f5a`.

This update fixes the three findings of the review of `05243edc5`.

1. A section with no `WATERJET` header after a waterjet section is refused by name.
   - The engine now sets the section's current properties before `onSection`. The hook no longer reads a header that the previous `ENDSECTION` cleared.
   - The post refuses a jet word or a cut with no header in `jetOk` (new `headerOk`). It never drops the motion without a warning.
   - Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_an_adjacent_section_with_no_header` (the review's input). The test checks the named refusal, the first section's `G1 X1 Y0 F300`, one nozzle comment and one `G54`.
2. Merge of upstream main `35940da16`. Conflicts resolved:
   - `engine.rs`: main's upright-after-tilt refusal and `machine::flatten` stay. `programBounds` is published after `set_machine`.
   - `mod.rs`: `machine_installation` and `machine_travel` both stay.
   - `comment_escape.rs`: main's native-Agie refusal check stays. The waterjet machine kind stays. The count is now `text_posts == 22` (23 shipped posts, 1 native refusal).
3. Quick gate on the final combined head: GREEN (below).

Mutation checks on pin 1:

- Engine refresh removed: RED (two nozzle comments).
- Engine refresh and post `headerOk` guard both removed: RED (no warning, the review's silent output).
- Both restored: GREEN.
- The post guard alone is a second guard. With the engine refresh in place, `startPreamble` refuses first, so the pin cannot isolate the post guard.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 1,131 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 20.4 minutes.
- Clippy (gate step, `-p` all nine selected crates, `--all-targets -- -D warnings`): GREEN.
- `adaptive_troch_parallel`: passed in 16 s in the gate. The earlier 90 s timing failure did not repeat.
- `comment_escape`, `waterjet_engine`, `waterjet_iso_post`, `script_waterjet_iso`: pass on the merged tree.
- The heavy lanes and the light lane did not run in this round. The reviewer's heavy run on `05243edc5` was GREEN.

The PR remains a draft. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

The sections below describe the original implementation and its historical validation. Their test counts and gate results are historical.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 996 steps, 0 failed (wall 30.5 min; the `cl` change reaches each dependent crate). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

title: feat(wire): post placed DXF racetracks and circles with native Agie arcs
body:
Stacked on #2974. Review the [placed DXF wire changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/760e62cc194f49d6efb51cfd557574d7df4cede0...80daeae0852e3f46a6ebfa5b47c13aeb2689b592).

**Safety review pending on `80daeae08`.** This branch predates the zero-step writer in #2951. The control results below describe the placed DXF profile on the tested installation. Before merge or machine use, this branch must adopt the #2984 correction and verify that the control imports the work with zero erosion steps.

Use one closed DXF racetrack or circle as the source for a vertical punch. Keep the original lines and arcs through placement, normal Wire Contour generation, verification and native output. Invalidate the toolpath when the source or placement changes. The conservative preview encloses the exact arcs with at most 0.000025 mm of radial excess.

A racetrack needs two parallel cardinal straight sides tangent to two semicircles. A circle needs a radius from 6 through 15 mm and a radial threading lead on a cardinal side. The native grid must represent the circle and the intended seam. Individual chain selection, other drawings and laser work remain part of #2022.

Run the original examples from the repository root:

```sh
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/racetrack.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/circle-punch.camscript
cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- script examples/agie/north-circle.camscript
```

The translated and 90 degree rotated R10 racetrack generated 1,409 moves with zero warnings. Agie Control kept the arc centers at (−6, 1) and (10, 1). It reported pass radii of 10.245, 10.155, 10.140 and 10.134 mm. The arc direction reversed on alternate passes. The separation on the straight section measured 1.000 mm.

On circular jobs, each bridge swept 1/R radians for a 1.000 mm nominal arc. The rough and trim wire paths stayed concentric. Three CAMCraft jobs exercised R6 east, R10 west and R15 north. Separate synthetic reference jobs checked all four cardinal directions at R10. The formal checks reported zero job errors. The control requested machining and reference setup and reported option 131072. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 24 scoped app tests, 15 native post tests and both round-profile geometry tests. Strict Clippy passed for the app, geometry and post libraries. In the integrated feature branch, all 13 example jobs and three additional stock heights exported correctly. All 50 files matched their earlier verified output. Each repeat export preserved every file.

Effort: high
Changelog: Placed DXF racetracks and circles can drive a verified Wire Contour punch and produce native Agie arcs from the original drawing.

Refs #2022

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |
| project: the key is read | `mcp_sets_the_group_...` | red |
| motion: entered mode refused (`Guards::source`) | `each_guard_is_pinned_...` | red |
| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |
| motion: the allowance grows the material (`Guards::allowance`) | same | red |
| motion: the film of the reading (one cell diagonal put back) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.
The first run of the two stamp mutants and of the bad-value mutant stayed green on the app tests, because another path gave the same result. I added the two lib pins for them, and the mutants are red on those pins.

This head is a clean merge of `upstream/main` `1e7800a9e` into `66c63889e`. The merge has no conflict and no hand edit.
Head `66c63889e` is the merge with `upstream/main` `b5ef7c39e`. That merge has hand edits in `generate.rs`, `rest_op_tests.rs` and `rest_adaptive_op.rs`. The [author comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2890#issuecomment-7090371248) describes them.
